340	
341	Faces already assigned to spherical hypotheses are excluded from seeds. Seeds with fewer than \`MIN_TORUS_FACES\` (7) faces or fewer than 9 unique vertices are skipped (torus has 7 DOF, needs sufficient data for a reliable fit). Returns a single seed per starting face.

343	**Surface fit**: Tries **two methods** and keeps whichever achieves the lowest maximum vertex-to-torus distance: (1) **Medial axis / tube center method**: estimates minor radius from normal-line intersections of adjacent face pairs, computes tube centers $k_i = p_i \pm r \cdot n_i$, fits a 3D circle to the tube centers for axis direction and major radius, then LM refinement of 7 parameters $[C_x, C_y, C_z, \alpha, \beta, R, r]$. (2) **SOR axis method**: estimates axis from PCA of vertex positions (smallest eigenvector), center via Kasa circle fit, radii from (h,r) profile circle fit, then same LM refinement. Rejects if minor_radius ≤ 0, major_radius ≤ 0, or minor_radius > major_radius (self-intersecting). See [SURFACE_FITTING.md](SURFACE_FITTING.md) for detailed fitting math.
344	
345	**Distance metric**: $|\sqrt{(\text{radial} - R)^2 + \text{axial}^2} - r|$ where $\text{axial} = (p - C) \cdot \hat{a}$ and $\text{radial} = |(p - C) - \text{axial} \cdot \hat{a}|$.
346	
347	**BFS-specific check — convexity**: Compute the vector from the nearest tube center point to the face centroid. Check that the face normal's dot product with this vector has the expected sign.

Normals — not centroid positions — are the decisive signal: a flat annulus or a cylinder band lies exactly on a one-parameter family of degenerate tori and can span a nonzero *positional* tube arc on a large-tube-radius member of that family, but its normals are all parallel (tube span ≈ 0).

353	#### 2.5 Select surfaces to use for reconstruction
354	Assign each mesh face to exactly one "selected surface" for reconstruction. Since stages 2.1–2.4 produce hypotheses that may overlap (a face can belong to one planar, one conical/cylindrical, one spherical, and one toroidal hypothesis simultaneously), surface selection must resolve these overlaps.
355	
356	
357	**Greedy area-based selection:**
358	
359	The algorithm selects hypotheses greedily by total mesh face area, largest first. This naturally resolves conflicts: real surface hypotheses cover many faces with large total area, while bogus hypotheses (e.g., a near-degenerate r=139mm sphere from 3 nearly-coplanar faces) cover minimal area and lose their faces to correctly-fitted surfaces.
360	
361	**Algorithm:**
362	1. Compute the geometric area of each mesh face.
363	2. Build a candidate list of all hypotheses (planar with face count > 1, conical/cylindrical, spherical, toroidal). Each candidate tracks its set of member faces and their total area.
364	
365	3. **Greedy loop**: while unassigned faces remain:
366	   a. For each candidate, compute the total area of its still-unassigned faces.
367	   b. Select the candidate with the largest remaining area.
368	   c. Assign all its still-unassigned faces to it as a selected surface.
369	   d. Remove those faces from all other candidates' pools.
370	4. Assign any remaining unassigned faces to their single-face planar hypothesis (fallback for faces on surfaces not yet fitted: ruled, freeform). Stage 2.7 may replace some of these with NURBS surfaces.
371	
372	5. Build a \`Vec<SelectedSurface>\`, one per selected hypothesis, containing:
373	   - \`surface_type: SurfaceType\` — enum: Planar, Cylindrical, Spherical, Conical, Toroidal (later: BSpline).
374	
375	   - \`hypothesis_index: usize\` — index into the appropriate hypothesis vector in Stage2Output.
376	   - \`faces: Vec<usize>\` — mesh face indices assigned to this surface.
377	   - \`vertices: Vec<usize>\` — mesh vertex indices on this surface (union of face vertices).
378	6. **Absorb redundant surfaces** (\`absorb_redundant_surfaces\`): merge a selected surface S into an adjacent, larger-area surface T when all of S's vertices lie within tolerance of T's fitted geometry AND all of S's face centroids lie within \`--surface-tolerance\` of T. Two situations require this:
379	   - *Spurious sub-fits*: a narrow band of faces on a cone/sphere can fit an "exact" cylinder (e.g. 3 azimuthal strips of a shallow cone have nearly coplanar normals) and get committed before the real surface's BFS reaches those faces. Tolerance: 10× vertex tolerance (exact overlap).
380	   - *Tangent-junction bridge facets*: a mesh facet spanning a tangent junction (e.g. cone–sphere on the nosecone) has vertices on both sides and can't be absorbed by either surface at vertex tolerance; it becomes an orphan single-face planar surface creating fake edges. Tolerance: \`--surface-tolerance\` (chordal sag), only for surfaces with ≤ 2 faces.
381	   The centroid check prevents absorbing flat end caps triangulated as a fan from a boundary vertex (all cap *vertices* lie on the adjacent cone/cylinder's boundary circle, but face interiors do not).
382	7. **Prune unselected hypotheses**: remove any hypothesis that was not selected from the hypothesis vectors in \`Stage2Output\`. Remap \`SelectedSurface\` indices to match the compacted vectors. After this step, \`Stage2Output.conical_hypotheses\` (etc.) contain only selected hypotheses.
383	8. Validate: every face is assigned to exactly one selected surface.
384	9. Print a summary: count of selected surfaces by type, total faces covered.
385	
386	**Why this works better than a fixed type-priority rule:** A fixed priority (e.g., spherical > cylindrical > multi-face planar) fails when a bogus hypothesis of a high-priority type (3-face r=139mm sphere) competes with a correct hypothesis of a lower-priority type (35-face r=2mm cylinder). Area-based greedy selection naturally picks the correct hypothesis because it covers vastly more area.

393	    - Compute face centroids and project them onto the selected surface.

397	#### 2.6 Surface refitting (boundary refinement — implemented)
398	
399	After selection and absorption, some border faces may have been absorbed by a hypothesis that fits within tolerance but isn't the best fit; the misassignment shifts the mesh region boundary by a row, which shifts reconstructed edge boundary vertices and corner vertices off the true feature curves.
400	
401	**Algorithm (\`refine_boundary_assignments\`, as implemented):**
402	1. Build the face → selected-surface map; walk every face that has a neighbor in a *different* selected surface (region-boundary faces — the original plan keyed on multi-hypothesis membership, but pruning/absorption destroy that; adjacency is the modern equivalent).
403	2. Compute the face's max vertex distance to its own surface and to each adjacent selected surface.
404	3. Move the face when an adjacent surface fits at least **2× better**. The margin prevents oscillation for true junction faces, whose vertices lie on both surfaces equally.
405	4. Iterate to a fixpoint (≤ 10 rounds; boundaries only move locally), then rebuild the affected hypotheses' vertex lists and drop emptied surfaces. Hypothesis *geometry* is not re-fitted: the fits were validated during BFS; only the region map changes.
406	
407	**Corner vertex refinement** (stage 3, \`refine_corner_vertices\`, runs after tangency detection): SHARP corner vertices are refined by cyclic projection onto their adjacent fitted surfaces — the raw mesh vertex at a corner is only as accurate as the tessellation puts it (where a fillet terminates, the mesh may have no vertex exactly at the CAD corner). Corners adjacent to any TANGENT edge are excluded: tangent surface pairs intersect along a curve rather than an isolated point, and cyclic projection slides along the tangent direction (observed drifting 0.57 mm). A safety guard keeps the original vertex if the refinement moves more than 2× surface tolerance.
408	
409	#### 2.7 NURBS fallback
410	
411	For groups of adjacent faces that remain as single-face planar hypotheses after stages 2.1–2.5 (i.e., they don't fit any analytic surface), try to fit a NURBS or B-spline surface.
412	
413	**Algorithm:**
414	1. Identify connected components of single-face planar hypothesis faces that are adjacent to each other in the mesh.
415	2. For each component with ≥ 4 faces:
416	   a. Compute UV parameterization of the face vertices (using discrete harmonic mapping or Floater's mean value coordinates).
417	   b. Use OCCT's \`GeomAPI_PointsToBSplineSurface\` to fit a B-spline through the parameterized points.
418	   c. Validate: max vertex-to-surface distance < \`--surface-tolerance\`.
419	   d. If valid, create a NURBS hypothesis; if not, leave as single-face planar.
420	3. Add valid NURBS hypotheses to the surface selection.
421	
422	*Comment: NURBS fitting is complex: parameterization quality strongly affects fit quality, degree/knot selection matters, and thin features may need special handling. Start with OCCT’s built-in B-spline fitter which handles degree selection and parameterization internally. For “freeform” regions that are nearly planar, a plane with small tolerance is preferable to a NURBS that overfits noise.*
423	
424	*Reconstruction note: the stage-3 shared-edge assembly rework (§3.x) is implemented and is the intended foundation for this stage. To reconstruct NURBS faces, extend \`SurfaceChart\` with a B-spline chart (point→UV via \`ShapeAnalysis_Surface::ValueOfUV\`, point_at via \`Geom_Surface::Value\`) and add the B-spline arm to \`create_occt_surface\`; the sampling/loop/winding/pcurve/wire machinery in stage 3.4 is surface-type-agnostic and needs no changes for non-periodic B-spline patches.*
425	
426	**Implementation notes for the NURBS pass** (knowledge from the stage-3 rework, 2026-07-08 — read before starting):
427	
428	- *The chart contract.* A chart provides \`point_uv(p) → (u, v, pole_radius)\` and \`point_at(u, v)\`, plus \`u_periodic()\`/\`v_periodic()\`. For a B-spline chart: \`pole_radius\` is ∞ (like the plane chart — fitted height-field patches have no UV degeneracies), and **both periodic flags must be false**. Every mod-2π unwrap/branch-lift in stage 3.4 is gated on those flags; reducing non-periodic parameter coordinates mod 2π silently corrupts them (this was a real bug on plane charts, masked for months by adaptive densification — see LEARNINGS). With both flags false, the whole seam/winding/degenerate-pole machinery self-disables and B-spline faces take the plain-loop path end to end.
429	- *The chart must wrap the exact \`Handle(Geom_BSplineSurface)\` stored in \`FaceDescriptor.surface\`* — never a reconstruction. (Analytic charts get away with rebuilding the gp_Ax3 only because that construction is deterministic.) Use one \`ShapeAnalysis_Surface\` per face: \`new_handlegeomsurface\` + \`value_of_uv(&mut self, pnt, precision)\` — note \`&mut\` (it caches internally). For sampling along an edge curve, prefer \`next_value_of_uv(prev_uv, pnt, preci, maxpreci)\` — it seeds the search from the previous sample, the B-spline analog of the analytic charts' branch-continuity unwrap. Validate each solution with \`gap()\` (ValueOfUV can return a poor projection rather than failing) and fall back to a fresh \`value_of_uv\` when the gap exceeds tolerance.
430	- *Every \`match\` on \`SelectedSurface\` needs a \`BSpline\` arm.* From crawling all of them: \`create_occt_surface\` and \`surface_faces\` (3.1), \`surface_normal_at_point\` (3.2 tangency detection and the 3.4 orientation compare — use D1 cross product on the handle), \`project_point_to_selected\` (corner-vertex refinement), \`build_face_chart\`, the concave-flag matches in \`assemble_face\`/\`create_occt_faces_all\`, the tangent-edge dispatch in 3.3, and the cosmetic \`stype\` labels + viz overlays.
431	- *Fix the fitted patch's normal orientation at fit time.* The shell orientation of a face comes from a single \`concave\` flag (natural surface normal vs. material). \`GeomAPI_PointsToBSplineSurface\` follows the orientation of the input point grid, so build the grid such that d1u×d1v matches the mesh's outward normals — then B-spline faces are always \`concave = false\`/FORWARD and tangency-detection normals need no sign logic. Choosing the convention at fit time is one line; recovering it later is a per-face heuristic.
432	- *Edge curves will lean on the boundary chain.* Expect \`GeomAPI_IntSS\` to be flakier against B-spline surfaces than between quadrics, and expect tangent-classified junctions (a fitted patch usually meets its neighbors near-tangentially) to have no analytic construction — both routes end at the mesh-boundary-chain machinery (\`repair_edge_curve_from_boundary\`, \`edge_curve_from_boundary_chain\`), which is surface-pair-agnostic. The one known extension needed: the chain repair currently fits only a line or a circle through the chain; genuinely freeform junctions need a third arm that fits a B-spline curve through the chain vertices (\`GeomAPI_PointsToBSpline\`, binding verified) with the same accept-if-it-fits-the-chain-better rule. The repair already degrades gracefully (keeps the better curve), so this can be added when the first freeform-junction model demands it.
433	- *What NURBS will not stress — don't build for it:* seams, winding loops, degenerate pole edges, seam-anchor planning, and edge splitting all apply only to periodic/wrapped faces; non-periodic B-spline patches never take those paths.
434	- *Bindings verified present (2026-07-08):* \`geom_api::PointsToBSplineSurface\` (grid constructor \`new_array2ofpnt_int2_shape_real\`), \`geom_api::PointsToBSpline\` (curve fit), \`shape_analysis::Surface::{new_handlegeomsurface, value_of_uv, next_value_of_uv, gap}\`, \`geom::BSplineSurface\`; the generic \`geom::Surface::{u_iso, v_iso, bounds, d0, d1}\` all work on B-splines.
435	- *Test models: DONE (2026-07-09), in \`tests/nurbs/\` — 8 STL/STEP pairs from \`gen-test-models\` (src/bin/gen_test_models.rs); see tests/nurbs/README.md for the difficulty ladder.* The original sketch (fit reference STEPs with \`PointsToBSplineSurface\` from sampled height-field grids) was rejected: the recognizer itself will use OCCT's fitters, so fitted references are circular (shared biases cancel) and only approximate. Instead every reference is EXACT — explicit-pole \`Geom_BSplineSurface\` lattices, conic/B-spline extrusions (\`Geom_SurfaceOfLinearExtrusion\`), and booleans of those. The doubly-curved patch models ship scripted regular-grid STLs sampled exactly on the reference surface (vertices on-surface to f32 precision); the ruled/extruded models (elliptical_arch, elliptical_cylinder, bspline_wave) deliberately ship as STRIP meshes — full-length strips with NO interior vertices along the ruling, exactly what real CAD exporters emit for extrusions — so the fitter must be designed for 2-ring sampling along a ruling (e.g. a ruled / low-v-degree fit) rather than assuming grid-like point coverage. The conic models' strips come from genuine OCCT tessellation; the wave's are scripted, because BRepMesh internally grid-refines B-spline-based surfaces at any deflection/angle setting (conic extrusions it strips naturally). The \`--compare\` gates are hard errors (volume >1%, round-trip re-read, surface distance), so NURBS reconstruction gets real pass/fail coverage from the first model. Generator-side caveat worth remembering: neither BRepGProp quadrature is trustworthy alone on freeform faces — fixed-order Gauss is ~0.5% low on localized bicubic bumps and ~4e-5 off on B-spline extrusions, while the adaptive variant measured 4% HIGH on a boolean-trimmed extrusion sheet and 0.3% LOW on the same surface as a natural prism face; the generator validates B-rep volumes against the closed STL meshes (scripted ones directly, tessellated ones parsed back) and against machine-exact profile integrals where available.
436	
437	---
438	
439	### Algorithm Reference
440	
441	Surface fitting math details (plane fitting, cylinder fitting, sphere fitting, cone fitting, torus fitting) and algorithmic techniques (Unified SOR Framework, Gaussian Map Classification, Medial Axis / Tube Center Method, Quadric Fitting) are documented in [SURFACE_FITTING.md](SURFACE_FITTING.md).
442	
443	---
444	
445	### Stage 3: Surface Reconstruction
446	
447	Build OCCT B-Rep topology (faces, edges, vertices) from the selected surfaces. This is the most complex stage — surface intersections in 3D are numerically delicate, and small perturbations can cause large changes in intersection curves or cause them to disappear.
448	
449	**Core data structures:**
450	
451	A vector of \`FaceDescriptor\` structs, one per selected surface:
452	- \`selected_surface_idx: usize\` — Index into the selected surfaces from stage 2.6.
453	- \`surface: OwnedPtr<HandleGeomSurface>\` — Infinite OCCT surface, type-erased (created in 3.1).
454	- \`adjacent_faces: Vec<usize>\` — Indices of adjacent FaceDescriptors, ordered topologically around this face's boundary. A face may appear multiple times if it shares multiple edges with this face (e.g., a cylindrical face adjacent to itself via a seam edge).
455	- \`edge_indices: Vec<usize>\` — ReconEdge indices. \`edge_indices[i]\` is the edge between this face and \`adjacent_faces[i]\`.
456	- \`vertex_indices: Vec<usize>\` — BRepVertex indices at corners. \`vertex_indices[i]\` is the vertex between \`edge_indices[i]\` and \`edge_indices[(i+1) % N]\`.
457	- The \`TopoDS_Face\` objects built from these descriptors live in \`Stage3Output.faces\` (parallel to \`face_descriptors\`), populated in 3.4, with \`Stage3Output.concave_faces\` flagging faces whose natural normal points into the material.
458	
459	A vector of \`ReconEdge\` structs:
460	- \`face_indices: [usize; 2]\` — Indices of the two adjacent FaceDescriptors.
461	- \`vertex_indices: [usize; 2]\` — Indices of the two BRepVertices at each end. For closed-loop edges (no vertices), both are \`usize::MAX\`.
462	- \`curve_3d: Option<OwnedPtr<HandleGeomCurve>>\` — 3D intersection curve, trimmed to vertex endpoints (populated in 3.3).
463	- \`pcurves: [Option<OwnedPtr<HandleGeom2dCurve>>; 2]\` — pcurve on each adjacent face's surface, parallel to \`face_indices\` (populated in 3.4 by the shared-edge assembler).
464	- \`tangent: bool\` — Whether the adjacent surfaces are tangent along this edge (detected in 3.2).
465	- \`mesh_boundary_vertices: Vec<usize>\` — Mesh vertex indices along this boundary, ordered along the boundary.
466	
467	A vector of \`BRepVertex\` structs:
468	- \`point: [f64; 3]\` — 3D position: the mesh vertex position, refined for sharp corners by cyclic projection onto the adjacent fitted surfaces (see stage 2.6 refitting notes).
469	- \`adjacent_faces: Vec<usize>\` — Indices of FaceDescriptors meeting at this vertex, in topological order.
470	- \`adjacent_edges: Vec<usize>\` — Indices of ReconEdges meeting at this vertex, in topological order.
471	- \`uv_coords: Vec<(f64, f64)>\` — UV coordinates of this vertex on each adjacent face's surface, parallel to \`adjacent_faces\` (populated in 3.4).
472	- Per-vertex tolerances live on the shared \`TopoDS_Vertex\` objects, raised adaptively in 3.4 to cover each vertex's distance from its curve endpoints.
473	
474	#### 3.1 Create OCCT surface objects and build adjacency graph
475	
476	**Surface creation** (\`create_occt_surface\`):
477	- For each selected surface, create the corresponding infinite OCCT surface:
478	    - Planar → \`geom::Plane::new_pnt_dir\` with \`gp::Pnt\` at centroid and \`gp::Dir\` along normal. Wrapped via \`to_handle().to_handle_surface()\`.
479	    - Cylindrical → \`geom::CylindricalSurface::new_ax3_real\` with \`gp::Ax3\` from axis origin/direction and radius. Wrapped via \`to_handle().to_handle_surface()\`.
480	    - Spherical → \`geom::SphericalSurface::new_ax3_real\` with \`gp::Ax3\` from center and Z-axis direction. Wrapped via \`to_handle().to_handle_surface()\`.
481	    - Conical → \`geom::ConicalSurface::new_ax3_real2\` with \`gp::Ax3\` from apex/direction and half-angle + radius at reference height. Wrapped via \`to_handle().to_handle_surface()\`. The \`Ax3\` origin is at the cone apex, Z along axis.
482	    - Toroidal → \`geom::ToroidalSurface::new_ax3_real2\` with \`gp::Ax3\` from center/axis direction, major radius $R$, and minor radius $r$. Wrapped via \`to_handle().to_handle_surface()\`. The \`Ax3\` origin is at the torus center, Z along rotation axis.
483	    - (Future: BSpline → \`Geom_BSplineSurface\` via \`GeomAPI_PointsToBSplineSurface\`.)
484	
485	- For consistency with OCCT conventions: planes use gp_Ax3 with Z as normal; cylinders have Z along axis; spheres have poles at Z extremes; cones have Z along axis from apex; tori have Z along rotation axis. This affects pcurve computation in 3.3.
486	
487	
488	**Adjacency graph construction:**
489	1. Build face-to-surface map: for each mesh face, record which selected surface it belongs to (\`build_face_to_surface_map\`).
490	2. Collect boundary edges: walk all mesh edges; when an edge separates faces belonging to different surfaces, record it as an \`UndirectedEdge\` keyed by \`SurfacePair\` (\`collect_boundary_edges\`).
491	3. Chain boundary edges: for each surface pair, chain connected boundary edges into ordered vertex sequences (\`chain_boundary_edges\`). Each chain becomes a \`ReconEdge\` with the mesh boundary vertices in order.
492	4. Find corner vertices: mesh vertices where 3+ selected surfaces meet become \`BRepVertex\` entries (\`find_corner_vertices\`). Their 3D position is taken from the mesh vertex.
493	5. Assign vertex indices to edges: for each \`ReconEdge\`, check if its first/last mesh boundary vertex is a corner vertex and set \`vertex_indices\` accordingly (or \`usize::MAX\` for closed-loop edges).
494	6. Build face descriptors: for each selected surface, create a \`FaceDescriptor\` with the OCCT surface handle. Walk the boundary edges, ordering them topologically around the face boundary (\`walk_edges_around_face\`). This uses a rotation-order algorithm: at each vertex, pick the next edge that rotates counter-clockwise around the face. This populates \`adjacent_faces\`, \`edge_indices\`, and \`vertex_indices\` for each face.
495	7. Build vertex adjacency: for each \`BRepVertex\`, walk the edges meeting at that vertex in topological order, recording \`adjacent_faces\` and \`adjacent_edges\`.
496	8. Validate topology: check Euler's formula V-E+F=2 for genus-0 models.
497	
498	- With the \`--compare\` flag (runs after stage 3.2 tangency detection):
499	    - For each \`ReconEdge\`, sample the mesh boundary vertices along the edge. For each sample vertex, compute the distance to the nearest edge/vertex in the reference STEP file using \`BRepExtrema_DistShapeShape\`. Report an error if any sample exceeds the edge's tolerance: \`--vertex-tolerance\` for sharp edges, \`--surface-tolerance\` for tangent edges (an imprecise tessellation can place the region boundary one row off a tangent junction — still within chordal tolerance of both surfaces and harmless, since tangent junction curves are built from the fitted hypotheses, not from these vertices).
500	    - For each \`BRepVertex\`, compute the distance from the vertex's 3D position to the nearest vertex in the reference STEP file. Report an error if any exceeds \`--vertex-tolerance\`.
501	    - These checks validate that the adjacency graph's topological features (edges where surfaces meet, corners where 3+ surfaces meet) correspond to real features in the reference model.
502	
503	#### 3.2 Detect tangency relationships
504	For each ReconEdge, determine whether the two adjacent surfaces are tangent along the shared boundary. This matters because \`GeomAPI_IntSS\` can fail or produce degenerate results for tangent/near-tangent surfaces, requiring special handling in edge curve computation (3.3).
505	
506	**Detection algorithm (implemented):**
507	- For each ReconEdge, sample mesh boundary vertices along the shared boundary (every 5th vertex, minimum 3 samples, always including first and last).
508	- At each sample point, compute the outward-facing surface normal of both adjacent surfaces analytically:
509	    - Planar: the hypothesis normal (constant).
510	    - Cylindrical: normalized radial direction from axis to point, negated if concave.
511	    - Spherical: normalized direction from center to point, negated if concave.
512	    - Conical: radial direction from axis at the point's axial position, rotated by the cone's half-angle away from the axis, negated if concave. Specifically: for point $p$ with axial component $h = (p-A)\cdot\hat{a}$, the normal is the unit vector in the plane of (radial, axis) at angle $(90° - \theta)$ from radial.
513	    - Toroidal: direction from the nearest tube center point to the surface point, negated if concave. The tube center is $c = C + R \cdot \hat{r}$ where $\hat{r}$ is the radial unit vector from the torus axis to the point.
514	
515	- Compute the dot product of the two normals. If all sampled pairs agree within 2° (dot > cos(2°) ≈ 0.9994), mark the edge as tangent.
516	- Points too close to a cylinder axis or sphere center (degenerate) cause the edge to be marked non-tangent.
517	
518	**Decision: do not modify surfaces to enforce tangency.** Modifying analytic surfaces would change the geometry. Instead, tangent edges get special handling in edge curve computation (3.3): construct the edge curve directly rather than relying on surface-surface intersection.
519

1	# NURBS Recognizer Test Models
2	
3	Targets for the DEVELOPMENT_PLAN §2.7 NURBS fallback. Every model contains at
4	least one surface outside brepper's analytic set (plane / cylinder / sphere /
5	cone / torus), so **all of these are expected to FAIL full \`--compare\` until
6	§2.7 lands** — they are the goal posts for that work, listed in RESULTS.md as
7	their own group. Stage 1 (mesh validity and STL↔STEP vertex agreement) passes
8	today and is covered by \`stage1_integration.rs\`.
9	
10	Regenerate with \`./scripts/generate_occt_models.sh\` (see
11	\`src/bin/gen_test_models.rs\`).
12	
13	## Construction principles
14	
15	- **Exact references, no fitting.** Every STEP is built from exact geometry:
16	  explicit-pole \`Geom_BSplineSurface\` lattices, conic / B-spline extrusions,
17	  and booleans of those. The recognizer will use OCCT fitting APIs
18	  (\`GeomAPI_PointsToBSplineSurface\`), so a fitted reference would be circular
19	  (shared biases cancel) and only approximate. Here the reference *is* ground
20	  truth.
21	- **Two mesh styles, both from the exact geometry.** The doubly-curved patch
22	  models ship scripted regular-grid STLs with vertices sampled exactly on
23	  the reference surface (measured ≤2e-6 mm, i.e. f32 STL quantization; see
24	  \`step-measure-tolerance\`) — the cleanest possible fitter input. The
25	  ruled/extruded models (\`elliptical_arch\`, \`elliptical_cylinder\`,
26	  \`bspline_wave\`) arrive as full-length STRIP meshes with no interior
27	  vertices along the ruling — how CAD exporters actually tessellate
28	  extrusions. That is deliberate: the NURBS recognizer has to handle real
29	  exports, so it gets built against strip meshes from day one instead of
30	  conveniently gridded ones. The conic models' strips come from genuine
31	  OCCT tessellation; the wave's are scripted (vertices exactly on the
32	  curve) because BRepMesh internally grid-refines B-spline-based surfaces
33	  at any deflection/angle setting. \`hill_with_hole\` is a plain OCCT
34	  tessellation — one realistically irregular CAD-export-style mesh.
35	- **Slab models** (\`bspline_*\`): the exact surface overhangs a box footprint
36	  (pole lattice padded beyond it); the solid is Cut(box, Prism(surface face))
37	  so walls and bottom are box planes and the top is the untouched exact
38	  surface. The generator validates every written STL by parsing it back:
39	  closed oriented manifold, and divergence-theorem volume against the B-rep.
40	  (Neither BRepGProp quadrature variant alone is trustworthy on freeform
41	  faces: fixed-order Gauss is ~0.5% low on bspline_hill's bump and ~4e-5
42	  off on B-spline extrusions; the adaptive variant measured 4% high on a
43	  boolean-trimmed extrusion sheet and 0.3% low on the same surface as a
44	  natural prism face. The generator accepts agreement with either, plus a
45	  machine-exact profile integral for the wave.)
46	
47	## Models (increasing recognizer difficulty)
48	
49	| Model | Freeform surface | Exercises |
50	|-------|------------------|-----------|
51	| elliptical_arch | half-ellipse (15×8) linear extrusion, 20 long | Simplest target: one non-periodic singly-curved patch, sharp 90° boundaries, planar neighbors. Strip mesh: 2 vertex rings along the extrusion. |
52	| bspline_hill | bicubic patch, Gaussian-shaped 15×15 pole lattice | Canonical doubly-curved dome on a slab; smooth curvature decay into near-flat corners (plane-absorption risk at loose tolerance). |
53	| bspline_saddle | bicubic patch, hyperbolic-paraboloid pole net | Negative Gaussian curvature everywhere (only torus inner regions have it today). |
54	| bspline_wave | cubic B-spline profile extruded along Y | Curvature sign alternates; crest/trough radii ≈3 mm are cylinder-detector bait — the over-segmentation trap. Strip mesh across Y. |
55	| bspline_terrain | bicubic patch: bump + dip + diagonal ripple | Multi-feature single patch; curvature varies in sign and magnitude. |
56	| bspline_blister | bicubic patch, raised poles only near center | Outer pole rings flat ⇒ margin is EXACTLY planar (B-spline local support), C² tangent join to the bump: segmentation boundary is ambiguous, junction curve is freeform. |
57	| hill_with_hole | bspline_hill minus off-center vertical cylinder r=5 | Freeform × analytic interaction: inner loop on the B-spline face, cylinder∩B-spline edge curves, irregular tessellated mesh. |
58	| elliptical_cylinder | full ellipse (12×7) prism, 18 tall | Stretch case: closed periodic freeform wall needs a periodic B-spline face + seam (out of scope for the first §2.7 pass). Strip mesh: full-height wall strips. |
59	
60	Current failure mode (recorded 2026-07-09): stage 2 leaves each freeform
61	region as single-face planar hypotheses (39 surfaces for the elliptical_arch
62	strip mesh, 53 for bspline_wave, 935 for the gridded bspline_hill) and the
63	stage 3.1 compare hard-errors with reconstructed vertices up to millimeters
64	from the reference. The strip-mesh models fail fast (~1 s); the dense grid
65	patches take ~35–105 s (bspline_hill ~104 s, near the 120 s run_test_table
66	timeout). Both will drop once stage 2.7 collapses those regions into single
67	surfaces.

307	/// Compute the area of a triangular mesh face.
308	pub(crate) fn face_area(face: &MeshFace, vertices: &[MeshVertex]) -> f64 {
309	    let v0 = &vertices[face.vertex_indices[0]];
310	    let v1 = &vertices[face.vertex_indices[1]];
311	    let v2 = &vertices[face.vertex_indices[2]];
312	    let ax = v1.x - v0.x;
313	    let ay = v1.y - v0.y;
314	    let az = v1.z - v0.z;
315	    let bx = v2.x - v0.x;
316	    let by = v2.y - v0.y;
317	    let bz = v2.z - v0.z;
318	    let cx = ay * bz - az * by;
319	    let cy = az * bx - ax * bz;
320	    let cz = ax * by - ay * bx;
321	    let mut area = 0.5 * (cx * cx + cy * cy + cz * cz).sqrt();
322	    if face.vertex_count == 4 {
323	        let v3 = &vertices[face.vertex_indices[3]];
324	        let dx = v3.x - v0.x;
325	        let dy = v3.y - v0.y;
326	        let dz = v3.z - v0.z;
327	        let ex = by * dz - bz * dy;
328	        let ey = bz * dx - bx * dz;
329	        let ez = bx * dy - by * dx;
330	        area += 0.5 * (ex * ex + ey * ey + ez * ez).sqrt();
331	    }
332	    area
333	}
334	
335	/// Compute the face centroid for a mesh face.
336	pub(crate) fn face_centroid(face: &MeshFace, vertices: &[MeshVertex]) -> [f64; 3] {
337	    let n = face.vertex_count as usize;
338	    let mut cx = 0.0_f64;
339	    let mut cy = 0.0_f64;
340	    let mut cz = 0.0_f64;
341	    for vi_idx in 0..n {
342	        let v = &vertices[face.vertex_indices[vi_idx]];
343	        cx += v.x;
344	        cy += v.y;
345	        cz += v.z;
346	    }
347	    let inv_n = 1.0 / n as f64;
348	    [cx * inv_n, cy * inv_n, cz * inv_n]
349	}

353	    let len = (v[0] * v[0] + v[1] * v[1] + v[2] * v[2]).sqrt();
354	    if len > 0.0 {
355	        v[0] /= len;
356	        v[1] /= len;
357	        v[2] /= len;
358	    }

45	/// Lower bound on cross product magnitude |n₁ × n₂| for a valid cylinder/sphere
46	/// seed pair. Since |n₁ × n₂| = sin(θ) for unit normals, this corresponds to a
47	/// minimum dihedral angle of arcsin(0.01) ≈ 0.57° (~0.6°). Seed pairs closer
48	/// than this are too nearly parallel for numerically stable axis estimation
49	/// (cylinders) or sphere fitting (spheres). Together with \`angular_tol\` (the
50	/// upper bound, typically 17.5°), this defines the valid seed-pair window
51	/// [~0.6°, angular_tol].
52	pub(crate) const MIN_CROSS_THRESHOLD: f64 = 0.01;
53	
54	/// Fast-reject multiplier for BFS vertex-distance checks. When a candidate face
55	/// has a vertex farther than \`REFIT_SKIP_MULTIPLIER × vertex_tol\` from the
56	/// current fitted surface, the distance is too large for a re-fit to absorb and
57	/// the face is rejected immediately without attempting re-fitting.
58	/// Set to 10.0 to allow aggressive refitting — the refit itself validates all
59	/// faces, so the only cost of a high multiplier is more refit attempts.
60	pub(crate) const REFIT_SKIP_MULTIPLIER: f64 = 10.0;
61	
62	/// Minimum number of mesh faces required to accept a cylindrical hypothesis.
63	/// Any real CAD tessellation of a cylinder produces at least 3 facets around
64	/// the circumference; this rejects spurious 2-face fits (e.g. adjacent torus
65	/// facets that locally approximate a cylinder).
66	pub(crate) const MIN_CYLINDER_FACES: usize = 3;
67	
68	/// Minimum number of mesh faces required to accept a spherical hypothesis.
69	/// Sphere fitting has 4 degrees of freedom (cx, cy, cz, r), so at least 4
70	/// non-degenerate faces are needed for a well-determined fit. This also rejects
71	/// spurious fits from small patches that are consistent with many surface types.
72	pub(crate) const MIN_SPHERE_FACES: usize = 4;
73	
74	/// Minimum number of mesh faces required to accept a conical hypothesis.
75	/// A cone has 5 degrees of freedom (apex xyz, axis direction 2, half-angle),
76	/// so at least 6 faces are needed for a well-determined and robust fit.
77	pub(crate) const MIN_CONE_FACES: usize = 6;
78	
79	/// Minimum number of mesh faces required to accept a toroidal hypothesis.
80	/// A torus has 7 degrees of freedom (center xyz, axis direction 2, R, r),
81	/// so at least 7 faces are needed for a well-determined fit.
82	pub(crate) const MIN_TORUS_FACES: usize = 7;
83	
84	/// Maximum sphere radius as a multiple of the mesh bounding-box diagonal.
85	/// With solid-angle coverage validation and surface-tolerance validation during
86	/// BFS, this no longer needs to be tight — those checks prevent pathological
87	/// growth. A large value serves as a numerical guardrail against degenerate fits.
88	pub(crate) const MAX_SPHERE_RADIUS_FACTOR: f64 = 1000.0;
89	
90	/// Minimum eigenvalue ratio for solid-angle coverage validation.
91	/// Centroid-to-center direction vectors of a genuine spherical hypothesis span
92	/// 3D, so all eigenvalues of their covariance matrix are substantial.
93	/// Fillet-strip growth produces nearly coplanar directions (λ₃ ≈ 0).
94	pub(crate) const MIN_SPHERE_EIGENVALUE_RATIO: f64 = 0.01;

925	/// Distance from a mesh vertex to a selected surface's fitted geometry.
926	fn vertex_distance_to_selected(
927	    v: &MeshVertex,
928	    surface: &SelectedSurface,
929	    planar_hypotheses: &[PlanarHypothesis],
930	    conical_hypotheses: &[ConicalHypothesis],
931	    spherical_hypotheses: &[SphericalHypothesis],
932	    toroidal_hypotheses: &[ToroidalHypothesis],
933	) -> f64 {
934	    match surface {
935	        SelectedSurface::Planar(i) => {
936	            let h = &planar_hypotheses[*i];
937	            (h.normal[0] * v.x + h.normal[1] * v.y + h.normal[2] * v.z - h.distance).abs()
938	        }
939	        SelectedSurface::Conical(i) => {
940	            let h = &conical_hypotheses[*i];
941	            if h.is_cylinder() {
942	                cylindrical::vertex_to_cylinder_distance(
943	                    v, &h.apex, &h.axis_direction, h.radius_at_apex,
944	                ).abs()
945	            } else {
946	                conical::vertex_to_cone_distance(
947	                    v, &h.apex, &h.axis_direction, h.half_angle,
948	                ).abs()
949	            }
950	        }
951	        SelectedSurface::Spherical(i) => {
952	            let h = &spherical_hypotheses[*i];
953	            spherical::vertex_to_sphere_distance(v, &h.center, h.radius).abs()
954	        }
955	        SelectedSurface::Toroidal(i) => {
956	            let h = &toroidal_hypotheses[*i];
957	            toroidal::vertex_to_torus_distance(
958	                v, &h.center, &h.axis_direction, h.major_radius, h.minor_radius,
959	            ).abs()
960	        }
961	    }
962	}

964	/// Refine surface assignments at region boundaries (DEVELOPMENT_PLAN §2.6
965	/// "Surface refitting"). BFS greedily absorbs border faces that fit within
966	/// tolerance but belong more naturally to the adjacent surface — e.g. a face
967	/// one row past a fillet junction absorbed by the plane. The misassignment
968	/// shifts the mesh region boundary by a row, which shifts reconstructed edge
969	/// boundary vertices and corner vertices off the true feature curves.
970	///
971	/// For each face on a region boundary, compare the max vertex distance to
972	/// its own surface against each adjacent selected surface, and move the face
973	/// when an adjacent surface fits at least 2× better. The margin prevents
974	/// oscillation for true junction faces (whose vertices lie on both surfaces
975	/// equally). Iterates to a fixpoint (boundaries only ever move locally).

4123	fn sample_edge_uv(
4124	    edge: &topo_ds::Edge,

2157	/// Construct a line-based tangent edge curve (plane-cylinder, cylinder-cylinder, fallback).
2158	fn compute_tangent_edge_curve_line(
2159	    edge: &mut ReconEdge,
2160	    v0: &BRepVertex,
2161	    v1: &BRepVertex,
2162	    ss0: &SelectedSurface,
2163	    ss1: &SelectedSurface,
2164	    stage2: &Stage2Output,
2165	    config: &Config,
2166	) -> Result<(), String> {
2167	    // Get the line direction. For plane-CYLINDER (and cylinder-cylinder)
2168	    // tangencies the line is parallel to the cylinder axis. For plane-CONE
2169	    // tangencies the line is a cone GENERATOR — tilted from the axis by the
2170	    // half-angle — and the two endpoint vertices lie exactly on it, so the
2171	    // vertex-to-vertex direction is used (radius_at_apex is 0 for cones, so
2172	    // the analytic cylinder construction would collapse onto the axis).
2173	    let conical_is_cylinder = |idx: &usize| stage2.conical_hypotheses[*idx].is_cylinder();
2174	    let line_dir = match (ss0, ss1) {
2175	        (SelectedSurface::Conical(idx), SelectedSurface::Planar(_))
2176	        | (SelectedSurface::Planar(_), SelectedSurface::Conical(idx))
2177	            if conical_is_cylinder(idx) =>
2178	        {
2179	            let hyp = &stage2.conical_hypotheses[*idx];
2180	            hyp.axis_direction
2181	        }
2182	        (SelectedSurface::Conical(idx), SelectedSurface::Conical(_))
2183	            if conical_is_cylinder(idx) =>
2184	        {
2185	            let hyp = &stage2.conical_hypotheses[*idx];
2186	            hyp.axis_direction
2187	        }
2188	        _ => {
2189	            // Cone generators and general fallback: direction between the
2190	            // vertex endpoints.
2191	            let dx = v1.point[0] - v0.point[0];
2192	            let dy = v1.point[1] - v0.point[1];
2193	            let dz = v1.point[2] - v0.point[2];
2194	            let len = (dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz).sqrt();
2195	            if len < 1e-15 {
2196	                return Err("tangent edge has zero-length vertex span".to_string());
2197	            }
2198	            [dx / len, dy / len, dz / len]
2199	        }

1759	/// Maximum distance from a spread of the edge's mesh boundary vertices to
1760	/// the (trimmed) curve.
1761	fn boundary_chain_deviation(
1762	    curve: &geom::HandleGeomCurve,
1763	    mesh_boundary_vertices: &[usize],
1764	    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
1765	) -> f64 {
1766	    let n = mesh_boundary_vertices.len();
1767	    let step = (n / 9).max(1);
1768	    let mut dev = 0.0_f64;
1769	    for i in (0..n).step_by(step).chain([n - 1]) {
1770	        let v = &mesh.vertices[mesh_boundary_vertices[i]];
1771	        let pt = gp::Pnt::new_real3(v.x, v.y, v.z);
1772	        let proj = geom_api::ProjectPointOnCurve::new_pnt_handlegeomcurve(&pt, curve);
1773	        if proj.nb_points() == 0 {
1774	            // No projection: measure against the endpoints instead.
1775	            let c = curve.get();
1776	            let (p, q) = (c.value(c.first_parameter()), c.value(c.last_parameter()));
1777	            let dp = ((v.x - p.x()).powi(2) + (v.y - p.y()).powi(2) + (v.z - p.z()).powi(2)).sqrt();
1778	            let dq = ((v.x - q.x()).powi(2) + (v.y - q.y()).powi(2) + (v.z - q.z()).powi(2)).sqrt();
1779	            dev = dev.max(dp.min(dq));
1780	        } else {
1781	            dev = dev.max(proj.lower_distance());
1782	        }
1783	    }
1784	    dev
1785	}

13	///
14	/// Uses \`step_control::StepReader\` which holds the global STEP I/O mutex
15	/// for its entire lifetime, serializing access to OCCT's non-thread-safe
16	/// STEP reader state.
17	pub fn read_step_file(path: &str) -> Result<OwnedPtr<topo_ds::Shape>, String> {
18	    let mut reader = step_control::StepReader::new();
19	    let status = reader.read_file_charptr(path);

22	    }
23	    let progress = message::ProgressRange::new();

26	}

28	/// Write a shape to a STEP file.
29	///
30	/// Uses \`step_control::StepWriter\` which holds the global STEP I/O mutex
31	/// for its entire lifetime, serializing access to OCCT's non-thread-safe
32	/// STEP writer state (including \`Interface_Static\` settings).
33	pub fn write_step_file(shape: &topo_ds::Shape, path: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
34	    interface::Static::set_c_val("write.step.schema", "AP214");
35	    interface::Static::set_c_val("write.step.product.name", "brepper");
36	    let mut writer = step_control::StepWriter::new();
37	    let progress = message::ProgressRange::new();
38	    let status = writer.transfer_shape_stepmodeltype_bool_progressrange(
39	        shape,
40	        step_control::StepModelType::Asis,
41	        true,
42	        &progress,
43	    );
44	    if status != if_select::ReturnStatus::Retdone {
45	        return Err(format!("STEPControl_Writer::Transfer returned {status:?}"));
46	    }
47	    let status = writer.write(path);
48	    if status != if_select::ReturnStatus::Retdone {
49	        return Err(format!("STEPControl_Writer::Write returned {status:?}"));
50	    }
51	    Ok(())
52	}

54	/// Suppress OCCT's default console output (transfer statistics, etc.).
55	/// Replaces the default stdout printer with one that only prints Fail-level messages.
56	pub fn suppress_occt_messages() {
57	    let mut messenger_handle = message::default_messenger();
58	    let messenger = messenger_handle.get_mut();
59	    // Remove the default PrinterOStream (which prints to stdout)
60	    let type_desc = message::PrinterOStream::get_type_descriptor();
61	    messenger.remove_printers(type_desc);
62	    // Add a printer that only shows failures
63	    let printer = message::PrinterOStream::new_gravity(message::Gravity::Fail);
64	    let printer_handle = message::PrinterOStream::to_handle(printer);
65	    let printer_base = printer_handle.to_handle_printer();
66	    messenger.add_printer(&printer_base);
67	}

#!/bin/bash
# Run all STL test files through brepper and generate tests/RESULTS.md
# Usage: ./scripts/run_test_table.sh [<brepper_binary>]
# Default binary: ./target/release/brepper

set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

BREPPER="${1:-./target/release/brepper}"

if [ ! -x "$BREPPER" ]; then
    echo "Error: brepper binary not found at $BREPPER" >&2
    echo "Build with: cargo build --release" >&2
    exit 1
fi

OUTPUT="tests/RESULTS.md"

# Map STL file to its corresponding STEP file
find_step() {
    local stl="$1"
    local dir=$(dirname "$stl")
    local base=$(basename "$stl" .stl)

    # Strip .ascii suffix if present
    base="${base%.ascii}"

    # Try exact match first
    if [ -f "$dir/$base.step" ]; then
        echo "$dir/$base.step"
        return
    fi

    # Strip resolution suffixes (_coarse, _medium, _fine, _low, _high)
    local stripped=$(echo "$base" | sed -E 's/_(coarse|medium|fine|low|high)$//')
    if [ -f "$dir/$stripped.step" ]; then
        echo "$dir/$stripped.step"
        return
    fi

    echo ""
}

# Special flags for specific tests
get_extra_flags() {
    local stl="$1"
    case "$stl" in
        *rounded_cube_10_r2_coarse*)
            echo "--angular-tolerance 20"
            ;;
        *)
            echo ""
            ;;
    esac
}

# Count totals
total=0
pass_count=0
fail_count=0

//! Integration tests for Stage 2: surface fitting.
//!
//! Tests that planar hypothesis deduction produces correct results for
//! known planar models, and that --compare validation passes.

use brepper::config;
use brepper::{stage1, stage2};
use opencascade_sys::{b_rep_adaptor, geom_abs, gp, top_abs, top_exp, topo_ds};

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Helpers
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

fn manifest_dir() -> String {
    env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR").to_string()
}

fn config_for_stl(stl_path: &str) -> config::Config {
    config::parse_config_from(["brepper", stl_path, "--stage=2.1", "-q"]).unwrap()
}

fn config_for_compare(stl_path: &str, step_path: &str) -> config::Config {
    let mut config =
        config::parse_config_from(["brepper", stl_path, "--compare", step_path, "--stage=2.1", "-q"])
            .unwrap();
    config.load_compare_step().unwrap();
    config
}
fn config_for_stl_stage22(stl_path: &str) -> config::Config {
    config::parse_config_from(["brepper", stl_path, "--stage=2.2", "-q"]).unwrap()
}

fn config_for_compare_stage22(stl_path: &str, step_path: &str) -> config::Config {
    let mut config =
        config::parse_config_from(["brepper", stl_path, "--compare", step_path, "--stage=2.2", "-q"])
            .unwrap();
    config.load_compare_step().unwrap();
    config
}

/// Run stages 1 and 2.1, returning the Stage2Output.
fn run_stage2(config: &config::Config) -> stage2::Stage2Output {
    let mesh = stage1::stage1(config).expect("stage1 should pass");
    stage2::stage2(config, mesh, None).expect("stage2 should pass")
}

/// Get cylinder hypotheses from the unified conical_hypotheses vector.
fn cylinder_hypotheses(output: &stage2::Stage2Output) -> Vec<&stage2::ConicalHypothesis> {
    output.conical_hypotheses.iter().filter(|h| h.is_cylinder()).collect()
}

/// Check if a selected surface is a cylinder.
fn is_selected_cylinder(s: &stage2::SelectedSurface, output: &stage2::Stage2Output) -> bool {
    match s {
        stage2::SelectedSurface::Conical(i) => output.conical_hypotheses[*i].is_cylinder(),
        _ => false,
    }
}

/// Check if a selected surface is a true cone (not a cylinder).
fn is_selected_cone(s: &stage2::SelectedSurface, output: &stage2::Stage2Output) -> bool {
    match s {
        stage2::SelectedSurface::Conical(i) => !output.conical_hypotheses[*i].is_cylinder(),
        _ => false,
    }
}

/// Compute the centroid of a mesh face.
fn face_centroid(face: &stage1::MeshFace, vertices: &[stage1::MeshVertex]) -> [f64; 3] {
    let n = face.vertex_count as usize;
    let mut cx = 0.0_f64;
    let mut cy = 0.0_f64;
    let mut cz = 0.0_f64;
    for vi in 0..n {
        let v = &vertices[face.vertex_indices[vi]];
        cx += v.x;
        cy += v.y;
        cz += v.z;
    }
    let inv_n = 1.0 / n as f64;

//! Stage 3: Surface Reconstruction
//!
//! 3.1: Create OCCT surface objects from hypotheses and build adjacency graph
//! 3.2: Detect and create tangency relationships
//! 3.3: Create OCCT edge wires (surface-surface intersections)
//! 3.4: Create OCCT faces (surface bounded by wires)
//! 3.5: Construct shells from connected faces
//! 3.6: Construct solids from shells

use crate::config::Config;
use crate::stage1::{ConnectedMesh, MeshVertex};
use crate::stage2::{SelectedSurface, Stage2Output};
use crate::stage1;
use opencascade_sys::{
    b_rep, b_rep_adaptor, b_rep_bnd_lib, b_rep_builder_api, b_rep_check, b_rep_extrema,
    b_rep_g_prop, b_rep_lib,
    bnd, extrema,
    geom, geom2d, geom2d_api, geom_api, g_prop, gp, message, shape_analysis,
    shape_fix,
    t_col_std, t_colgp, top_abs, top_exp, top_loc, topo_ds, OwnedPtr,
};
use std::collections::{BTreeSet, HashMap, HashSet};
use std::time::Instant;
use std::error::Error;
use std::fmt::{Display, Formatter};

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Data structures — Stage 3 output
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Descriptor for a reconstructed B-Rep face, corresponding to one selected surface hypothesis.
pub struct FaceDescriptor {
    /// Index of the selected surface (into Stage2Output.selected_surfaces).
    pub selected_surface_idx: usize,
    /// OCCT surface object (Geom_Plane, Geom_CylindricalSurface, or Geom_SphericalSurface),
    /// type-erased as HandleGeomSurface.
    pub surface: OwnedPtr<geom::HandleGeomSurface>,
    // The TopoDS_Face objects built from these descriptors live in
    // Stage3Output.faces (parallel to face_descriptors), populated in 3.4.
    /// Indices of adjacent FaceDescriptors, ordered topologically around this face's boundary.
    /// A face connecting to this one via multiple edges will appear multiple times.
    pub adjacent_faces: Vec<usize>,
    /// ReconEdge indices, one per adjacent face. \`edge_indices[i]\` is the edge between
    /// this face and \`adjacent_faces[i]\`.
    pub edge_indices: Vec<usize>,
    /// BRepVertex indices at corners. \`vertex_indices[i]\` is the vertex between
    /// \`edge_indices[i]\` and \`edge_indices[(i+1) % N]\`.
    pub vertex_indices: Vec<usize>,
}

impl std::fmt::Debug for FaceDescriptor {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        f.debug_struct("FaceDescriptor")
            .field("selected_surface_idx", &self.selected_surface_idx)
            .field("surface", &"<HandleGeomSurface>")
            .field("adjacent_faces", &self.adjacent_faces)
            .field("edge_indices", &self.edge_indices)
            .field("vertex_indices", &self.vertex_indices)
            .finish()
    }

18	/// Fit a plane to a set of faces using area-weighted normal averaging and
19	/// vertex centroid for the distance.
20	pub(super) fn fit_plane(
21	    face_indices: &[usize],
22	    vertex_set: &HashSet<usize>,
23	    faces: &[MeshFace],
24	    vertices: &[MeshVertex],
25	) -> ([f64; 3], f64) {
26	    let mut sum_nx = 0.0_f64;
27	    let mut sum_ny = 0.0_f64;
28	    let mut sum_nz = 0.0_f64;
29	
30	    for &fi in face_indices {
31	        let face = &faces[fi];
32	        let n = face.normal.unwrap();
33	        let area = face_area(face, vertices);
34	        sum_nx += n[0] * area;
35	        sum_ny += n[1] * area;
36	        sum_nz += n[2] * area;
37	    }
38	
39	    let len = (sum_nx * sum_nx + sum_ny * sum_ny + sum_nz * sum_nz).sqrt();
40	    let normal = [sum_nx / len, sum_ny / len, sum_nz / len];
41	
42	    let mut sum_d = 0.0_f64;
43	    for &vi in vertex_set {
44	        let v = &vertices[vi];
45	        sum_d += normal[0] * v.x + normal[1] * v.y + normal[2] * v.z;
46	    }
47	    let distance = sum_d / vertex_set.len() as f64;
48	
49	    (normal, distance)
50	}

pub fn check_result<T>(result: OcctResult<T>) -> T {
    if !result.exc.is_null() {
        wrapper_threw_exception(result.exc);
    }
    result.ret
}

/// Check a void FFI result; panic if there was an exception.
#[inline(always)]
#[track_caller]
pub fn check_void_result(exc: *const std::ffi::c_char) {
    if !exc.is_null() {
        wrapper_threw_exception(exc);
    }
}

/// Called from C++ to allocate a null-terminated copy of the exception message.
///
/// The C++ side formats "TypeName: message" and passes it here.
/// We copy into Rust-allocated memory so \`wrapper_threw_exception\`
/// can free it with the Rust allocator.
