/// Fill grid nodes not covered by the region (hole interiors) with a
/// Laplacian membrane over the grid graph, so the B-spline approximator
/// sees smooth data there.
```

**After:**
```
/// Monotone reparameterizations of the two UV axes that equalize 3D arc
/// spacing. The Floater map compresses high-curvature areas, so sampling a
/// UV-uniform grid gives wildly uneven 3D point spacing; OCCT parameterizes
/// the fit by chord length *averaged across rows*, and locally
/// near-coincident stations make the interpolation system oscillate between
/// nodes (observed ~1 mm bulges on the saddle with all node residuals at
/// 1e-2). Sampling at arc-length-equalized stations keeps the fit's
/// parameterization consistent with the data everywhere.
struct AxisMaps {
    /// (uv, arc_fraction) samples of each axis's averaged cumulative arc
    /// profile G — strictly monotone.
    u_profile: Vec<(f64, f64)>,
    v_profile: Vec<(f64, f64)>,
}

impl AxisMaps {
    fn build(sampler: &UvSampler) -> AxisMaps {
        AxisMaps {
            u_profile: axis_profile(sampler, true),
            v_profile: axis_profile(sampler, false),
        }
    }

    /// Sample stations for `n` grid nodes along an axis: uv values whose
    /// arc fractions are uniform.
    fn stations(profile: &[(f64, f64)], n: usize) -> Vec<f64> {
        let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(n);
        let mut k = 0usize;
        for i in 0..n {
            let t = i as f64 / (n - 1) as f64;
            while k + 1 < profile.len() && profile[k + 1].1 < t {
                k += 1;
            }
            let (u0, g0) = profile[k];
            let (u1, g1) = profile[(k + 1).min(profile.len() - 1)];
            let s = if g1 > g0 { (t - g0) / (g1 - g0) } else { 0.0 };
            out.push((u0 + s.clamp(0.0, 1.0) * (u1 - u0)).clamp(0.0, 1.0));
        }
        out
    }

    /// Arc fraction G(uv) along an axis (for projection seeding: the fit's
    /// parameter is ~linear in arc fraction, not in raw UV).
    fn arc_fraction(profile: &[(f64, f64)], uv: f64) -> f64 {
        let mut k = 0usize;
        while k + 1 < profile.len() && profile[k + 1].0 < uv {
            k += 1;
        }
        let (u0, g0) = profile[k];
        let (u1, g1) = profile[(k + 1).min(profile.len() - 1)];
        let s = if u1 > u0 { (uv - u0) / (u1 - u0) } else { 0.0 };
        (g0 + s.clamp(0.0, 1.0) * (g1 - g0)).clamp(0.0, 1.0)
    }
}

/// Cumulative 3D arc profile of one UV axis, averaged over several isolines
/// of the other axis, normalized to [0, 1] and made strictly monotone. A
/// 15% blend with the identity bounds the distortion correction, keeping
/// stations well-defined where probe isolines cross data gaps.
fn axis_profile(sampler: &UvSampler, u_axis: bool) -> Vec<(f64, f64)> {
    const PROBES: usize = 9;
    const FINE: usize = 257;
    let mut cum = vec![0.0_f64; FINE];
    for pi in 0..PROBES {
        let w = pi as f64 / (PROBES - 1) as f64;
        let mut prev: Option<[f64; 3]> = None;
        for (k, c) in cum.iter_mut().enumerate().skip(1) {
            let t = k as f64 / (FINE - 1) as f64;
            let p = if u_axis {
                sampler.sample(t, w)
            } else {
                sampler.sample(w, t)
            };
            if let Some(p) = p {
                if let Some(q) = prev {
                    *c += ((p[0] - q[0]).powi(2) + (p[1] - q[1]).powi(2)
                        + (p[2] - q[2]).powi(2))
                    .sqrt();
                }
                prev = Some(p);
            }
        }
        // Make cum cumulative across k (each entry currently holds only its
        // own segment).
        for k in 1..FINE {
            cum[k] += cum[k - 1] - if k >= 2 { cum[k - 2] } else { 0.0 };
        }
    }
    // The loop above double-accumulates; rebuild cleanly instead.
    let mut segs = vec![0.0_f64; FINE];
    for pi in 0..PROBES {
        let w = pi as f64 / (PROBES - 1) as f64;
        let mut prev: Option<[f64; 3]> = None;
        for (k, s) in segs.iter_mut().enumerate() {
            let t = k as f64 / (FINE - 1) as f64;
            let p = if u_axis {
                sampler.sample(t, w)
            } else {
                sampler.sample(w, t)
            };
            if let Some(p) = p {
                if let Some(q) = prev {
                    *s += ((p[0] - q[0]).powi(2) + (p[1] - q[1]).powi(2)
                        + (p[2] - q[2]).powi(2))
                    .sqrt();
                }
                prev = Some(p);
            }
        }
    }
    let mut profile = Vec::with_capacity(FINE);
    let mut acc = 0.0_f64;
    for (k, s) in segs.iter().enumerate() {
        if k > 0 {
            acc += s;
        }
        profile.push((k as f64 / (FINE - 1) as f64, acc));
    }
    let total = acc.max(1e-30);
    for (u, g) in profile.iter_mut() {
        *g = 0.85 * (*g / total) + 0.15 * *u;
    }
    profile
}

/// Fill grid nodes not covered by the region (hole interiors) with a
/// Laplacian membrane over the grid graph, so the B-spline approximator
/// sees smooth data there.
```

/// One fit attempt at a fixed grid resolution: resample, orient, fit,
/// validate against `--surface-tolerance`.
fn fit_grid(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    region: &Region,
    sampler: &UvSampler,
    n_u: usize,
    n_v: usize,
    config: &Config,
) -> Result<BSplineHypothesis, String> {
    let mut grid: Vec<Option<[f64; 3]>> = Vec::with_capacity(n_u * n_v);
    for i in 0..n_u {
        for j in 0..n_v {
            let u = i as f64 / (n_u - 1) as f64;
            let v = j as f64 / (n_v - 1) as f64;
            grid.push(sampler.sample(u, v));
        }
    }

                }
            }
        }
        eprintln!(
            "  Stage 2.7: {}/{} grid nodes missing, first few at {:?}",
            grid.len() - covered,
            grid.len(),
            &missing_uvs[..missing_uvs.len().min(8)],
        );
    }

#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
fn validate_fit(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    region: &Region,
    uv: &[(f64, f64)],

    surface: OwnedPtr<geom::HandleGeomBSplineSurface>,
    n_u: usize,
    n_v: usize,
    grid: &[[f64; 3]],
    config: &Config,
) -> Result<BSplineHypothesis, String> {

    let tol = config.surface_tolerance_mm;
    // The fit's v axis is reversed when the grid was flipped for outward
    // orientation.
    let seed_of = |vi: usize| -> (f64, f64) {
        let (u, v) = uv[region.local[&vi]];
        (u, if flip { 1.0 - v } else { v })
    };
```

**After:**
```
#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
fn validate_fit(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    region: &Region,
    uv: &[(f64, f64)],
    maps: &AxisMaps,
    flip: bool,
    surface: OwnedPtr<geom::HandleGeomBSplineSurface>,
    n_u: usize,
    n_v: usize,
    grid: &[[f64; 3]],
    config: &Config,
) -> Result<BSplineHypothesis, String> {
    let mut hyp = BSplineHypothesis::new(surface, region.faces.clone(), region.verts.clone());
    let tol = config.surface_tolerance_mm;
    // The fit's parameter is ~linear in arc fraction (the grid stations
    // equalize arc), and its v axis is reversed when the grid was flipped
    // for outward orientation.
    let seed_of = |vi: usize| -> (f64, f64) {
        let (u, v) = uv[region.local[&vi]];
        let gu = AxisMaps::arc_fraction(&maps.u_profile, u);
        let gv = AxisMaps::arc_fraction(&maps.v_profile, v);
        (gu, if flip { 1.0 - gv } else { gv })
    };
```

/// Multi-face planar selections up to this many faces are candidates for
/// absorption into a freeform region they connect to smoothly. A smooth

const SMALL_PLANAR_ABSORB_FACES: usize = 4;

**After:**

/// Selections up to this many faces are candidates for absorption into a
/// freeform region they connect to smoothly. Freeform surfaces bait the
/// analytic detectors locally: an inflection produces short runs of
/// accidentally-coplanar facets fitted as tiny planes (bspline_wave), and
/// bands of near-constant curvature fit as narrow cylinder ribbons
/// (bspline_saddle: 16 six-face cylinders carving the patch apart). Left
/// selected, they punch holes in the freeform region. Real small features
/// are protected twice: a component with no single-face planar member is
/// never fitted, and absorbed non-single faces must not outnumber the
/// single-face leftovers (see `deduce_bspline_surfaces`).
const SMALL_SELECTION_ABSORB_FACES: usize = 8;
```

    let mut bspline_hypotheses: Vec<BSplineHypothesis> = Vec::new();

    // Stage 2.7: NURBS fallback — fit B-spline surfaces to connected
    // components of leftover single-face planar selections. This runs on
    // the raw selection, BEFORE absorption: the absorb pass legitimately
    // grows small accidental analytic fits (e.g. cylinder ribbons on a
    // freeform surface) with the exactly-on-surface facets around them,
    // which would hide them from the freeform region gathering.
    if config.stage.at_least(2, 7) {
        let viz_27 = if config.viz_active(2, 7) { viz } else { None };
        bspline::deduce_bspline_surfaces(
            &mesh, &mut selected_surfaces, &mut planar_hypotheses,
            &conical_hypotheses, &spherical_hypotheses, &toroidal_hypotheses,
            &mut bspline_hypotheses, viz_27, config,
        );
    }

    // Merge spurious sub-fit surfaces and tangent-junction orphan facets
    // into larger adjacent surfaces (including freshly fitted B-splines)
    // before reconstruction.
    absorb_redundant_surfaces(
        &mesh, &mut selected_surfaces, &mut planar_hypotheses,
        &mut conical_hypotheses, &mut spherical_hypotheses,
        &mut toroidal_hypotheses, &mut bspline_hypotheses, config,
    );

    // Move border faces to the adjacent surface that fits them better —
    // misassigned rows shift reconstructed edge/corner positions off the
    // true feature curves (DEVELOPMENT_PLAN §2.6 surface refitting).
    refine_boundary_assignments(
        &mesh, &mut selected_surfaces, &mut planar_hypotheses,
        &mut conical_hypotheses, &mut spherical_hypotheses,
        &mut toroidal_hypotheses, &bspline_hypotheses, config,
    );

            // B-spline surfaces are not move targets (same domain-extension
            // hazard as in absorption: the fit doesn't vouch for faces
            // outside the region it was built from).
            let mut candidates: Vec<usize> = face.neighbors[..vc]
                .iter()
                .filter(|&&ni| ni >= 0)
                .map(|&ni| face_to_surface[ni as usize])
                .filter(|&sj| {
                    sj != usize::MAX
                        && sj != si
                        && !matches!(selected_surfaces[sj], SelectedSurface::BSpline(_))
                })
                .collect();

/// Grid stations for one axis. When the two opposite boundary sides have
/// equal vertex counts (structured meshes: grids and strips), the stations
/// are the boundary vertices' own pinned positions (averaged between the
/// sides), subdivided to the target density — interpolation then passes
/// through on-surface data instead of chord interiors, whose corner-cutting
/// at profile kinks cost the coarse arch 1.7% of its volume. Unstructured
/// boundaries fall back to arc-length-uniform stations.
fn axis_stations(
    side_a: &[f64],
    side_b: &[f64],
    target: usize,
    profile: &[(f64, f64)],
) -> Vec<f64> {
    if side_a.len() != side_b.len() || side_a.len() < 2 {
        return AxisMaps::stations(profile, target);
    }
    let base: Vec<f64> = side_a
        .iter()
        .zip(side_b)
        .map(|(a, b)| ((a + b) / 2.0).clamp(0.0, 1.0))
        .collect();
    // Subdivide every interval evenly until the target count is met.
    let k = (target.saturating_sub(1)).div_ceil(base.len() - 1).max(1);
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity((base.len() - 1) * k + 1);
    for w in base.windows(2) {
        for step in 0..k {
            out.push(w[0] + (w[1] - w[0]) * step as f64 / k as f64);
        }
    }
    out.push(*base.last().unwrap());
    out
}

/// One fit attempt at fixed grid stations: resample, orient, fit,
/// validate against `--surface-tolerance`.
#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
fn fit_grid(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    region: &Region,
    sampler: &UvSampler,
    maps: &AxisMaps,
    u_stations: &[f64],
    v_stations: &[f64],
    config: &Config,
) -> Result<BSplineHypothesis, String> {
    let (n_u, n_v) = (u_stations.len(), v_stations.len());
    let mut grid: Vec<Option<[f64; 3]>> = Vec::with_capacity(n_u * n_v);
    for i in 0..n_u {

/// Validate an edge curve against the mesh boundary chain; on failure, try
/// the circle through three spread chain vertices (falling back to the
/// original curve when the chain is straight or the repair doesn't help).
fn repair_edge_curve_from_boundary(
    curve: OwnedPtr<geom::HandleGeomCurve>,
    edge: &ReconEdge,
    vertices: &[BRepVertex],
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    config: &Config,
    fi0: usize,
    fi1: usize,
) -> OwnedPtr<geom::HandleGeomCurve> {
    if edge.mesh_boundary_vertices.len() < 3 {
        return curve;
    }
    let tol = config.surface_tolerance_mm;
    let dev = boundary_chain_deviation(&curve, &edge.mesh_boundary_vertices, mesh);
    if dev <= tol {
        return curve;
    }

    // Fit the circle through three spread chain vertices.
    let chain = &edge.mesh_boundary_vertices;
    let pnt_at = |i: usize| {
        let v = &mesh.vertices[chain[i]];
        gp::Pnt::new_real3(v.x, v.y, v.z)
    };
    let (p0, p1, p2) = (pnt_at(0), pnt_at(chain.len() / 2), pnt_at(chain.len() - 1));
    let Some(circle) = reconstruct_full_circle(&p0, &p1, &p2) else {
        if !config.quiet {
            eprintln!(
                "  Warning: edge (f{fi0},f{fi1}) curve is {dev:.3} mm from its mesh \
                 boundary chain and the chain is straight — keeping the curve"
            );
        }
        return curve;
    };

    // Trim to the endpoint vertices with a chain-supported arc, or keep the
    // full circle for closed-loop edges.
    let repaired: Option<OwnedPtr<geom::HandleGeomCurve>> = if edge.vertex_indices[0] != usize::MAX
        && edge.vertex_indices[1] != usize::MAX
    {
        let v0 = &vertices[edge.vertex_indices[0]];
        let v1 = &vertices[edge.vertex_indices[1]];
        match (
            project_point_on_curve(&v0.point, &circle),
            project_point_on_curve(&v1.point, &circle),
        ) {
            (Ok(t0), Ok(t1)) => {
                let (t_lo, t_hi) =
                    select_arc_parameters(t0, t1, &edge.mesh_boundary_vertices, &circle, mesh);
                let arc = geom::TrimmedCurve::new_handlegeomcurve_real2(&circle, t_lo, t_hi);
                Some(geom::TrimmedCurve::to_handle(arc).to_handle_curve())
            }
            _ => None,
        }
    } else {
        Some(circle)
    };

    match repaired {
        Some(repaired) => {
            let new_dev =
                boundary_chain_deviation(&repaired, &edge.mesh_boundary_vertices, mesh);
            if new_dev < dev {
                if !config.quiet {
                    eprintln!(
                        "  Edge (f{fi0},f{fi1}): curve was {dev:.3} mm from its mesh boundary \
                         chain; repaired with the chain's circle ({new_dev:.2e} mm)"
                    );
                }
                if new_dev > tol && !config.quiet {
                    eprintln!(
                        "  Warning: edge (f{fi0},f{fi1}) repaired curve still {new_dev:.3} mm \
                         from its mesh boundary chain"
                    );
                }
                repaired
            } else {
                curve
            }
        }
        None => curve,
    }
}

/// Validate an edge curve against the mesh boundary chain; on failure, try
/// the circle through three spread chain vertices and a B-spline curve fit
/// through the whole chain, keeping whichever candidate deviates least
/// (genuinely freeform junctions — e.g. a fitted patch meeting a plane
/// along an elliptical profile — are neither lines nor circles).
fn repair_edge_curve_from_boundary(
    curve: OwnedPtr<geom::HandleGeomCurve>,
    edge: &ReconEdge,
    vertices: &[BRepVertex],
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    config: &Config,
    fi0: usize,
    fi1: usize,
) -> OwnedPtr<geom::HandleGeomCurve> {
    if edge.mesh_boundary_vertices.len() < 3 {
        return curve;
    }
    let tol = config.surface_tolerance_mm;
    let dev = boundary_chain_deviation(&curve, &edge.mesh_boundary_vertices, mesh);
    if dev <= tol {
        return curve;
    }

    let chain = &edge.mesh_boundary_vertices;
    let has_endpoints =
        edge.vertex_indices[0] != usize::MAX && edge.vertex_indices[1] != usize::MAX;

    // Trim a full repair curve to the edge's endpoint vertices (chain-
    // supported side for periodic candidates), or keep it whole for
    // closed-loop edges.
    let trim_to_endpoints = |full: &geom::HandleGeomCurve| -> Option<OwnedPtr<geom::HandleGeomCurve>> {
        if !has_endpoints {
            return None;
        }
        let v0 = &vertices[edge.vertex_indices[0]];
        let v1 = &vertices[edge.vertex_indices[1]];
        match (
            project_point_on_curve(&v0.point, full),
            project_point_on_curve(&v1.point, full),
        ) {
            (Ok(t0), Ok(t1)) => {
                let (t_lo, t_hi) = select_arc_parameters(t0, t1, chain, full, mesh);
                let arc = geom::TrimmedCurve::new_handlegeomcurve_real2(full, t_lo, t_hi);
                Some(geom::TrimmedCurve::to_handle(arc).to_handle_curve())
            }
            _ => None,
        }
    };

    let mut best_dev = dev;
    let mut best: Option<(OwnedPtr<geom::HandleGeomCurve>, &'static str)> = None;

    // Candidate 1: the circle through three spread chain vertices.
    let pnt_at = |i: usize| {
        let v = &mesh.vertices[chain[i]];
        gp::Pnt::new_real3(v.x, v.y, v.z)
    };
    let (p0, p1, p2) = (pnt_at(0), pnt_at(chain.len() / 2), pnt_at(chain.len() - 1));
    if let Some(circle) = reconstruct_full_circle(&p0, &p1, &p2) {
        let candidate = if has_endpoints {
            trim_to_endpoints(&circle)
        } else {
            Some(circle)
        };
        if let Some(c) = candidate {
            let d = boundary_chain_deviation(&c, chain, mesh);
            if d < best_dev {
                best_dev = d;
                best = Some((c, "circle"));
            }
        }
    }

    // Candidate 2: a B-spline curve through the chain vertices (open chains
    // only — the approximator is not periodic). The chain is ground truth
    // for any junction, so an ordered fit through it handles freeform
    // junction curves no analytic construction covers.
    if has_endpoints && chain.len() >= 4 {
        let mut pts = t_colgp::Array1OfPnt::new_int2(1, chain.len() as i32);
        for (k, &vi) in chain.iter().enumerate() {
            let v = &mesh.vertices[vi];
            let p = gp::Pnt::new_real3(v.x, v.y, v.z);
            pts.set_value(k as i32 + 1, &p);
        }
        let fit_tol = (config.surface_tolerance_mm / 10.0).max(config.vertex_tolerance_mm * 10.0);
        let fit = std::panic::catch_unwind(std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe(|| {
            geom_api::PointsToBSpline::new_array1ofpnt_int2_shape_real(
                &pts,
                3,
                8,
                geom_abs::Shape::C2,
                fit_tol,
            )
        }));
        if let Ok(fit) = fit {
            if fit.is_done() {
                let full = fit.curve().to_handle_curve();
                if let Some(c) = trim_to_endpoints(&full) {
                    let d = boundary_chain_deviation(&c, chain, mesh);
                    if d < best_dev {
                        best_dev = d;
                        best = Some((c, "B-spline"));
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }

    match best {
        Some((repaired, kind)) => {
            if !config.quiet {
                eprintln!(
                    "  Edge (f{fi0},f{fi1}): curve was {dev:.3} mm from its mesh boundary \
                     chain; repaired with the chain's {kind} ({best_dev:.2e} mm)"
                );
                if best_dev > tol {
                    eprintln!(
                        "  Warning: edge (f{fi0},f{fi1}) repaired curve still {best_dev:.3} mm \
                         from its mesh boundary chain"
                    );
                }
            }
            repaired
        }
        None => {
            if !config.quiet {
                eprintln!(
                    "  Warning: edge (f{fi0},f{fi1}) curve is {dev:.3} mm from its mesh \
                     boundary chain and no chain-based repair improved it — keeping the curve"
                );
            }
            curve
        }
    }
}

/// Grid stations for one axis. When the two opposite boundary sides have
/// equal vertex counts (structured meshes: grids and strips), the stations
/// are the boundary vertices' own pinned positions (averaged between the
/// sides), subdivided to the target density — interpolation then passes
/// through on-surface data instead of chord interiors, whose corner-cutting
/// at profile kinks cost the coarse arch 1.7% of its volume. Unstructured
/// boundaries fall back to arc-length-uniform stations.
fn axis_stations(
    side_a: &[f64],
    side_b: &[f64],
    target: usize,
    profile: &[(f64, f64)],
) -> Vec<f64> {
    if side_a.len() != side_b.len() || side_a.len() < 2 {
        return AxisMaps::stations(profile, target);
    }
    let base: Vec<f64> = side_a
        .iter()
        .zip(side_b)
        .map(|(a, b)| ((a + b) / 2.0).clamp(0.0, 1.0))
        .collect();
    // Stations sit exactly at the vertices: between vertices the sampler
    // returns chord points, and pinning the interpolant there reproduces
    // the chordal prism instead of a smooth surface through the vertices —
    // on the coarse arch that cost 1.7% of the volume, the exact size of
    // the mesh's own chordal deficit. Subdivide only up to the minimum
    // workable grid (linear data across a strip ruling stays exact).
    let min_stations = 8usize;
    let k = (min_stations.saturating_sub(1)).div_ceil(base.len() - 1).max(1);
    let _ = target; // density drives only the unstructured fallback path
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity((base.len() - 1) * k + 1);
    for w in base.windows(2) {
        for step in 0..k {
            out.push(w[0] + (w[1] - w[0]) * step as f64 / k as f64);
        }
    }
    out.push(*base.last().unwrap());
    out
}

/// Grid stations for one axis: the distinct parameter values of the
/// region's own vertices, so interpolation passes through on-surface data
/// wherever the mesh has it. Anything else backfires somewhere in the mesh
/// zoo: stations between the vertices of a coarse profile sample chord
/// interiors and reproduce the chordal prism (1.7% volume deficit on the
/// arch), while boundary-derived stations undersample interiors that are
/// denser than their boundary (an 8×8 grid for the 1719-face
/// hill_with_hole). Denser-than-cap meshes are quantile-subsampled (equal
/// vertex count per interval — matches the data density); sparser-than-
/// minimum axes (a strip mesh's 2-ring ruling) are subdivided evenly, which
/// is exact for their linear data.
fn axis_stations(values: &[f64], cap: usize) -> Vec<f64> {
    let mut sorted = values.to_vec();
    sorted.push(0.0);
    sorted.push(1.0);
    sorted.sort_by(|a, b| a.partial_cmp(b).unwrap());
    let mut distinct: Vec<f64> = Vec::new();
    for v in sorted {
        if distinct.last().is_none_or(|&l| v - l > 1e-9) {
            distinct.push(v.clamp(0.0, 1.0));
        }
    }
    if distinct.len() > cap {
        // Quantile subsample, always keeping the first and last.
        let d = distinct.len();
        return (0..cap)
            .map(|i| distinct[(i * (d - 1)) / (cap - 1)])
            .collect();
    }
    let min_stations = 8usize;
    if distinct.len() < min_stations {
        let k = (min_stations - 1).div_ceil(distinct.len() - 1).max(1);
        let mut out = Vec::with_capacity((distinct.len() - 1) * k + 1);
        for w in distinct.windows(2) {
            for step in 0..k {
                out.push(w[0] + (w[1] - w[0]) * step as f64 / k as f64);
            }
        }
        out.push(*distinct.last().unwrap());
        return out;
    }
    distinct
}

    /// Sample stations for `n` grid nodes along an axis: uv values whose
    /// arc fractions are uniform.
    fn stations(profile: &[(f64, f64)], n: usize) -> Vec<f64> {
        let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(n);
        let mut k = 0usize;
        for i in 0..n {
            let t = i as f64 / (n - 1) as f64;
            while k + 1 < profile.len() && profile[k + 1].1 < t {
                k += 1;
            }
            let (u0, g0) = profile[k];
            let (u1, g1) = profile[(k + 1).min(profile.len() - 1)];
            let s = if g1 > g0 { (t - g0) / (g1 - g0) } else { 0.0 };
            out.push((u0 + s.clamp(0.0, 1.0) * (u1 - u0)).clamp(0.0, 1.0));
        }
        out
    }

/// Grid stations for one axis. The base stations are the boundary
/// vertices' own pinned positions (averaged between the two opposite
/// sides — structured or not, the boundary is where the region has exact
/// on-surface data at exact parameters): stations *between* the vertices
/// of a coarse profile sample chord interiors and pin the interpolant to
/// the chordal prism (a 1.7% volume deficit on the arch, the mesh's own
/// chordal error). The base is then evenly subdivided up to the interior-
/// density target when the boundary is coarser than the region it bounds
/// (flat margins tessellate coarsely: hill_with_hole has 8-vertex sides on
/// a 946-vertex region, and an 8×8 grid cannot carry the bump). Sides with
/// mismatched vertex counts fall back to arc-length-uniform stations.
fn axis_stations(
    side_a: &[f64],
    side_b: &[f64],
    target: usize,
    profile: &[(f64, f64)],
) -> Vec<f64> {
    if side_a.len() != side_b.len() || side_a.len() < 2 {
        return AxisMaps::stations(profile, target);
    }
    let base: Vec<f64> = side_a
        .iter()
        .zip(side_b)
        .map(|(a, b)| ((a + b) / 2.0).clamp(0.0, 1.0))
        .collect();
    let k = (target.saturating_sub(1)).div_ceil(base.len() - 1).max(1);
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity((base.len() - 1) * k + 1);
    for w in base.windows(2) {
        for step in 0..k {
            out.push(w[0] + (w[1] - w[0]) * step as f64 / k as f64);
        }
    }
    out.push(*base.last().unwrap());
    out
}

/// Selections up to this many faces are candidates for absorption into a
/// freeform region they connect to smoothly. Freeform surfaces bait the
/// analytic detectors locally: an inflection produces short runs of
/// accidentally-coplanar facets fitted as tiny planes (bspline_wave), and
/// bands of near-constant curvature fit as narrow cylinder ribbons
/// (bspline_saddle: 16 six-face cylinders carving the patch apart). Left
/// selected, they punch holes in the freeform region. Real small features
/// are protected twice: a component with no single-face planar member is
/// never fitted, and absorbed non-single faces must not outnumber the
/// single-face leftovers (see `deduce_bspline_surfaces`).
const SMALL_SELECTION_ABSORB_FACES: usize = 8;

/// Selections up to this many faces are candidates for absorption into a
/// freeform region they connect to smoothly. Freeform surfaces bait the
/// analytic detectors locally: an inflection produces short runs of
/// accidentally-coplanar facets fitted as tiny planes (bspline_wave),
/// bands of near-constant curvature fit as narrow cylinder ribbons
/// (bspline_saddle: 16 six-face cylinders carving the patch apart), and a
/// Gaussian bump peak fits 9–12-face cones (hill_with_hole). Left
/// selected, they punch holes in the freeform region and leave fake
/// feature edges. Real small features are protected twice: a component
/// with no single-face planar member is never fitted, and absorbed
/// non-single faces must not outnumber the single-face leftovers (see
/// `deduce_bspline_surfaces`).
const SMALL_SELECTION_ABSORB_FACES: usize = 16;

cat >> ./tests/stage2_integration.rs <<'EOF'

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Stage 2.7: NURBS fallback (tests/nurbs models)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

fn config_for_compare_stage27(stl_path: &str, step_path: &str) -> config::Config {
    let mut config =
        config::parse_config_from(["brepper", stl_path, "--compare", step_path, "--stage=2.7", "-q"])
            .unwrap();
    config.load_compare_step().unwrap();
    config
}

/// Count selected surfaces by (planar, bspline); assert nothing else was
/// selected. Assertions are on stage 2.6 *selected* surfaces, per policy.
fn planar_bspline_selection_counts(output: &stage2::Stage2Output) -> (usize, usize) {
    let mut planar = 0;
    let mut bspline = 0;
    for s in &output.selected_surfaces {
        match s {
            stage2::SelectedSurface::Planar(_) => planar += 1,
            stage2::SelectedSurface::BSpline(_) => bspline += 1,
            other => panic!("unexpected selected surface type: {other:?}"),
        }
    }
    (planar, bspline)
}

/// elliptical_arch: one non-periodic singly-curved patch over a strip mesh
/// (2 vertex rings along the extrusion), plus bottom and two end walls.
#[test]
fn nurbs_elliptical_arch_stage27_selection() {
    let stl = format!("{}/tests/nurbs/elliptical_arch.stl", manifest_dir());
    let step = format!("{}/tests/nurbs/elliptical_arch.step", manifest_dir());
    let config = config_for_compare_stage27(&stl, &step);
    let output = run_stage2(&config);
    let (planar, bspline) = planar_bspline_selection_counts(&output);
    assert_eq!(bspline, 1, "arch surface should be one B-spline");
    assert_eq!(planar, 3, "bottom + two end walls");
    let hyp = &output.bspline_hypotheses[0];
    assert!(
        hyp.error_max <= config.surface_tolerance_mm,
        "fit must respect surface tolerance (got {})",
        hyp.error_max
    );
}

/// bspline_wave: alternating-curvature extrusion over a strip mesh. The
/// over-segmentation trap: accidental coplanar strip pairs at inflections
/// must be absorbed into the freeform region, not fragment it.
#[test]
fn nurbs_bspline_wave_stage27_selection() {
    let stl = format!("{}/tests/nurbs/bspline_wave.stl", manifest_dir());
    let step = format!("{}/tests/nurbs/bspline_wave.step", manifest_dir());
    let config = config_for_compare_stage27(&stl, &step);
    let output = run_stage2(&config);
    let (planar, bspline) = planar_bspline_selection_counts(&output);
    assert_eq!(bspline, 1, "wave surface should be one B-spline, not fragments");
    assert_eq!(planar, 5, "bottom + four walls");
}

/// chamfered_cube must be untouched by the NURBS fallback: every face is a
/// single-face planar selection (45° chamfer junctions are sharp, and no
/// component reaches the minimum size).
#[test]
fn nurbs_leaves_chamfered_cube_planar() {
    let stl = format!("{}/tests/onshape/chamfered_cube_10_c1_medium.stl", manifest_dir());
    let config = config::parse_config_from(["brepper", &stl, "--stage=2.7", "-q"]).unwrap();
    let output = run_stage2(&config);
    let (planar, bspline) = planar_bspline_selection_counts(&output);
    assert_eq!(bspline, 0, "no freeform surfaces on a chamfered cube");
    assert_eq!(planar, 26, "6 cube faces + 12 chamfers + 8 corner triangles");
}

For “freeform” regions that are nearly planar, a plane with small tolerance is preferable to a NURBS that overfits noise.*

To reconstruct NURBS faces, extend \`SurfaceChart\` with a B-spline chart (point→UV via \`ShapeAnalysis_Surface::ValueOfUV\`, point_at via \`Geom_Surface::Value\`) and add the B-spline arm to \`create_occt_surface\`; the sampling/loop/winding/pcurve/wire machinery in stage 3.4 is surface-type-agnostic and needs no changes for non-periodic B-spline patches.*
426:**Implementation notes for the NURBS pass** (knowledge from the stage-3 rework, 2026-07-08 — read before starting):
433:- *What NURBS will not stress — don't build for it:* seams, winding loops, degenerate pole edges, seam-anchor planning, and edge splitting all apply only to periodic/wrapped faces; non-periodic B-spline patches never take those paths.
435:- *Test models: DONE (2026-07-09), in \`tests/nurbs/\` — 8 STL/STEP pairs from \`gen-test-models\` (src/bin/gen_test_models.rs); see tests/nurbs/README.md for the difficulty ladder.* The original sketch (fit reference STEPs with \`PointsToBSplineSurface\` from sampled height-field grids) was rejected: the recognizer itself will use OCCT's fitters, so fitted references are circular (shared biases cancel) and only approximate. Instead every reference is EXACT — explicit-pole \`Geom_BSplineSurface\` lattices, conic/B-spline extrusions (\`Geom_SurfaceOfLinearExtrusion\`), and booleans of those. The doubly-curved patch models ship scripted regular-grid STLs sampled exactly on the reference surface (vertices on-surface to f32 precision); the ruled/extruded models (elliptical_arch, elliptical_cylinder, bspline_wave) deliberately ship as STRIP meshes — full-length strips with NO interior vertices along the ruling, exactly what real CAD exporters emit for extrusions — so the fitter must be designed for 2-ring sampling along a ruling (e.g. a ruled / low-v-degree fit) rather than assuming grid-like point coverage. The conic models' strips come from genuine OCCT tessellation; the wave's are scripted, because BRepMesh internally grid-refines B-spline-based surfaces at any deflection/angle setting (conic extrusions it strips naturally). The \`--compare\` gates are hard errors (volume >1%, round-trip re-read, surface distance), so NURBS reconstruction gets real pass/fail coverage from the first model. Generator-side caveat worth remembering: neither BRepGProp quadrature is trustworthy alone on freeform faces — fixed-order Gauss is ~0.5% low on localized bicubic bumps and ~4e-5 off on B-spline extrusions, while the adaptive variant measured 4% HIGH on a boolean-trimmed extrusion sheet and 0.3% LOW on the same surface as a natural prism face; the generator validates B-rep volumes against the closed STL meshes (scripted ones directly, tessellated ones parsed back) and against machine-exact profile integrals where available.
574:For each ReconFace, construct a \`TopoDS_Face\` from the surface and the shared edges — **shared-edge topological assembly** (the §3.x rework, implemented). Every ReconEdge is exactly one \`TopoDS_Edge\` used by both adjacent faces; each face attaches its own pcurve to the shared edge and assembles its wires and the face directly with \`BRep_Builder\`. \`MakeWire\`/\`MakeFace\`-from-wire/\`ShapeFix\` (which copy edges and would break the sharing) are not used; one uniform mechanism covers planes, cylinders, cones, spheres, and tori alike, and is the intended foundation for NURBS faces.
584:- Each face gets an analytic **chart** (\`SurfaceChart\`) mirroring the gp_Ax3 frame of its OCCT surface, with closed-form point→(U,V) and (U,V)→point maps for all five surface types (a future NURBS chart can substitute \`ShapeAnalysis_Surface::ValueOfUV\`). All UV work — sampling, windows, orientation tests — is analytic; \`GeomAPI_ProjectPointOnSurf\` is no longer used in face construction.
648:Result: full test suite green, \`cone_tangent_planes\` volume matches to ~1e-7 relative (was 60% off), \`stepped_block_toroidal_fillets\` volume improved (2.7e-3 → 1.6e-3 relative), and every remaining pole/seam behavior is a consequence of the uniform mechanism rather than a per-surface special case. The NURBS effort (§2.7) can now add freeform faces by supplying a chart (point→UV map) and reusing the whole assembler unchanged.
792:- [ ] Support for OBJ, PLY input formats
793:- [ ] IGES export option
794:- [ ] Hole detection and filling
795:- [ ] Feature recognition (holes, pockets, bosses)
796:- [ ] Curvature-based surface detection: use per-vertex principal curvatures (Rusinkiewicz estimator) as an alternative seeding signal. Principal curvature signatures: plane (k1≈k2≈0), sphere (k1≈k2, constant), cylinder (k1=const, k2≈0), cone (k1 varies, k2≈0), torus (k1=const, k2 varies).
797:- [ ] Quadric pre-classification: fit 10-coefficient quadric via SVD as a fast O(N) surface classifier before expensive nonlinear fitting. Eigenvalue pattern of the 3×3 quadric matrix directly classifies plane/sphere/cylinder/cone.
798:- [ ] Adaptive mesh density handling: current BFS tolerance assumes roughly uniform tessellation. For meshes with varying triangle density (e.g., adaptive refinement near features), weight BFS decisions by triangle area.
129:Supported stages: \`2.1\` (planar), \`2.2\` (cylindrical), \`2.3\` (spherical), \`2.4\` (conical), \`2.6\` (surface selection), \`3.3\` (edge curves), \`3.4\` (faces), \`3.5\` (shells), \`3.6\` (solids).

428	- *The chart contract.* A chart provides \`point_uv(p) → (u, v, pole_radius)\` and \`point_at(u, v)\`, plus \`u_periodic()\`/\`v_periodic()\`. For a B-spline chart: \`pole_radius\` is ∞ (like the plane chart — fitted height-field patches have no UV degeneracies), and **both periodic flags must be false**. Every mod-2π unwrap/branch-lift in stage 3.4 is gated on those flags; reducing non-periodic parameter coordinates mod 2π silently corrupts them (this was a real bug on plane charts, masked for months by adaptive densification — see LEARNINGS). With both flags false, the whole seam/winding/degenerate-pole machinery self-disables and B-spline faces take the plain-loop path end to end.
429	- *The chart must wrap the exact \`Handle(Geom_BSplineSurface)\` stored in \`FaceDescriptor.surface\`* — never a reconstruction. (Analytic charts get away with rebuilding the gp_Ax3 only because that construction is deterministic.) Use one \`ShapeAnalysis_Surface\` per face: \`new_handlegeomsurface\` + \`value_of_uv(&mut self, pnt, precision)\` — note \`&mut\` (it caches internally). For sampling along an edge curve, prefer \`next_value_of_uv(prev_uv, pnt, preci, maxpreci)\` — it seeds the search from the previous sample, the B-spline analog of the analytic charts' branch-continuity unwrap. Validate each solution with \`gap()\` (ValueOfUV can return a poor projection rather than failing) and fall back to a fresh \`value_of_uv\` when the gap exceeds tolerance.

#### 2.7 NURBS fallback

For groups of adjacent faces that remain as single-face planar hypotheses after stages 2.1–2.5 (i.e., they don't fit any analytic surface), try to fit a NURBS or B-spline surface.

**Algorithm:**
1. Identify connected components of single-face planar hypothesis faces that are adjacent to each other in the mesh.
2. For each component with ≥ 4 faces:
   a. Compute UV parameterization of the face vertices (using discrete harmonic mapping or Floater's mean value coordinates).
   b. Use OCCT's `GeomAPI_PointsToBSplineSurface` to fit a B-spline through the parameterized points.
   c. Validate: max vertex-to-surface distance < `--surface-tolerance`.
   d. If valid, create a NURBS hypothesis; if not, leave as single-face planar.
3. Add valid NURBS hypotheses to the surface selection.

*Comment: NURBS fitting is complex: parameterization quality strongly affects fit quality, degree/knot selection matters, and thin features may need special handling. Start with OCCT’s built-in B-spline fitter which handles degree selection and parameterization internally. For “freeform” regions that are nearly planar, a plane with small tolerance is preferable to a NURBS that overfits noise.*

**After:**
```markdown
#### 2.7 NURBS fallback (implemented 2026-07-10, `src/stage2/bspline.rs`)

For groups of adjacent faces that remain as single-face planar selections after selection (i.e., they fit no analytic surface), fit a B-spline surface. Runs on the raw selection, **before** `absorb_redundant_surfaces`: the absorb pass legitimately grows small accidental analytic fits (cylinder ribbons on a freeform surface) with the exactly-on-surface facets around them, which would hide them from region gathering. Absorption and boundary refinement run afterwards, with B-spline surfaces excluded as targets (the fit only vouches for the faces it was built from; a chordal absorb would extend the face into the surface's extrapolation zone).

**Algorithm (`deduce_bspline_surfaces`), as implemented:**
1. **Gather** connected components of single-face planar selections over SMOOTH mesh edges (face-normal step ≤ `--angular-tolerance` — a freeform surface varies by at most the tessellation's angular step between neighbors; a 45° chamfer junction is a real feature edge and must split components). The candidate set also includes selections of ≤ 16 faces of any type: freeform surfaces bait the analytic detectors locally (accidentally-coplanar strip pairs at wave inflections, 6-face cylinder ribbons carving up the saddle, 9–12-face cones on a Gaussian bump peak), and left selected they punch holes in the region and leave fake feature edges. Two guards protect real small features: a component with no single-face planar member is never fitted, and when absorbed non-single faces would outnumber the single-face leftovers the component is stripped back to the leftovers.
2. **Tangent-plane merge**: a multi-face planar selection whose *entire* shared boundary with a component is smooth is the flat part of the same freeform surface (B-spline local support makes exactly-planar margins — bspline_blister) and is merged in; keeping it separate invents a feature edge the reference doesn't have. Real planar neighbors (walls, bottoms) always meet freeform regions across at least some sharp edges. Analytic models are untouched — they have no ≥ 4-face freeform components.
3. Components below 4 faces stay single-face planar. Components planar to fitting exactness (10× vertex tolerance, NaN-guarded: the area-weighted normal of a closed region cancels to zero) become a multi-face planar hypothesis instead — a plane is preferable to a B-spline that overfits noise.
4. **Parameterize** the region onto the unit square: outer boundary loop pinned by cumulative chord length, 4 corners chosen where the adjacent *outside* selection changes (arc-length-quartile fallback when the boundary offers ≠ 4 transitions), interior and hole-loop vertices solved with Floater mean-value weights by Gauss–Seidel (convergence enforced — an unconverged map voids Floater's bijectivity guarantee). Quads are split along the v0–v2 diagonal for weighting and sampling.
5. **Resample a grid** through the flattened triangulation (uniform-bin point location; numeric misses near corner slivers are clamped to the nearest triangle within one bin — feeding them to the hole membrane extrapolates garbage). Grid stations per axis are the boundary vertices' own pinned positions (stations *between* the vertices of a coarse profile sample chord interiors and pin the fit to the chordal prism — a 1.7% volume deficit on the arch, the mesh's own chordal error), evenly subdivided up to an interior-density target of ~1.5·√(region vertices) (a flat margin tessellates coarsely: hill_with_hole has 8-vertex sides on a 946-vertex region). Genuine hole interiors are filled with a Laplacian membrane so the fitter sees smooth data. The grid is flipped if needed so d1u×d1v matches the mesh's outward normals: B-spline faces are always `concave = false`.
6. **Fit**: `GeomAPI_PointsToBSplineSurface::Interpolate` (chord-length, C2 cubic) first — the grid is sampled from an exact-on-surface mesh, and OCCT's least-squares approximator reports `IsDone` while overshooting its `Tol3D` by millimeters near strongly curved patch boundaries. The approximator (tol = surface/8, then surface/2) remains as fallback, and grid density retries at caps 121/181/241.
7. **Validate**: every region vertex and face centroid within `--surface-tolerance` of the fit, each projection seeded from the vertex's own parameterization value (sequential seeding breaks at mesh row wraps, and neither `NextValueOfUV` nor `ValueOfUV` recovers reliably on many-knot surfaces). On failure the component stays single-face planar with a warning.

The `BSplineHypothesis` owns the fitted `Geom_BSplineSurface` (stage 3 reuses the same object via fresh handles) plus a cached, seed-rechecking `ShapeAnalysis_Surface` projector used by absorption, refinement, `--compare`, and stage-3 charts/normals/projections.

**Results (2026-07-10)**: 7 of the 8 `tests/nurbs/` models pass full `--compare` (volume within 2.7e-6 … 5.2e-3 relative); `elliptical_cylinder` (closed periodic freeform wall needing a seam) remains out of scope, rejected cleanly at parameterization. Full 476-test suite green.

**Implementation notes for the NURBS pass** (knowledge from the stage-3 rework, 2026-07-08; all items below are now implemented as described — kept for reference):
```

region as single-face planar hypotheses (39 surfaces for the elliptical_arch
strip mesh, 53 for bspline_wave, 935 for the gridded bspline_hill) and the
stage 3.1 compare hard-errors with reconstructed vertices up to millimeters
from the reference. The strip-mesh models fail fast (~1 s); the dense grid
patches take ~35–105 s (bspline_hill ~104 s, near the 120 s run_test_table
timeout). Both will drop once stage 2.7 collapses those regions into single
surfaces.

**After:**
```markdown
Status (2026-07-10, §2.7 implemented): each freeform region collapses into a
single fitted B-spline surface (elliptical_arch: 4 selected surfaces
matching the reference's 4 faces; bspline_blister's exactly-planar margin is
tangent-merged into the freeform top, matching the reference topology).
Volumes agree with the exact references to 2.7e-6 … 5.2e-3 relative — well
inside the 1% hard gate. `elliptical_cylinder`'s wall is rejected cleanly at
parameterization (a closed wall flattens to an annulus, not a disk) and the
model still fails `--compare` as expected. The pre-2.7 failure mode — every
freeform region as hundreds of single-face planar surfaces, stage 3.1
hard-erroring with reconstructed vertices millimeters off — is gone, and the
dense grid models dropped from ~35–105 s to the cost of stage 2's analytic
BFS passes (~60 s, dominated by cylinder/torus seeding, not by §2.7).

# Brepper - STL to STEP Converter

Convert triangulated STL meshes from CAD exports into parametric STEP files with fitted analytic and freeform surfaces.

## Usage

\`\`\`
brepper - Convert STL mesh to STEP with fitted surfaces

USAGE:
    brepper [OPTIONS] <input.stl> [-o <output.step>]

REQUIRED:
    <input.stl>              Input STL file (binary or ASCII)

GENERAL OPTIONS:
    -o <step>, --output=<step>  Output STEP file
    --stl-units=<units>      Units used by the STL file (mm, cm, m, in, ft, um; default: mm)
    --step-units=<units>     Units to use in exported STEP file (default: mm)
    --compare=<step>         STEP file to compare to at each step
    --vertex-tolerance=<value>  Fitting tolerance in STL units (default: 5e-5)
    --surface-tolerance=<value> Surface-to-face offset tolerance in STL units (default: 0.4)
    --angular-tolerance=<deg>   Max dihedral angle between adjacent triangles on the same surface (default: 25)
    -v, --verbose[=LEVEL]    Verbosity level: 1 = stage summaries, 2 = per-hypothesis details,
                             3 = commit details/stats/profiles, 4 = per-seed details, 5 = BFS face trace
    -q, --quiet              Suppress non-error output
    --debug                  Enable debug output and intermediate files
    --stage=<stage>          Stop after stage, e.g. 2.2 (default: 4.1). --stage=2 stops after all of stage2
    --viz-stages=<stages>    Open interactive 3D visualization at specified stages (e.g. 2.1,2.2,2.3)
    --viz-stages-level=<N>   Viz detail level: 1 = committed hypotheses (default), 2 = seeds, 3 = BFS faces
```
</details>

```
Stage 2.7 NURBS fallback: freeform regions become fitted B-spline faces

Implements DEVELOPMENT_PLAN §2.7. Connected components of leftover
single-face planar selections are parameterized with Floater mean-value
coordinates (boundary chord-pinned to the unit square, corners at
outside-selection transitions), resampled on a grid whose stations follow
the mesh's own vertices, fitted with GeomAPI_PointsToBSplineSurface
(interpolation first, approximation fallback, density retries), and
validated vertex-by-vertex against --surface-tolerance. Fitted surfaces
flow through stage 3 via a new B-spline SurfaceChart wrapping the exact
fitted Geom_BSplineSurface with a cached ShapeAnalysis_Surface projector;
the seam/winding/pole machinery self-disables (both periodic flags false),
and grids are oriented at fit time so B-spline faces are always
concave=false.

Design decisions forced by the models (each a measured failure first):

- Stage 2.7 runs BEFORE absorb_redundant_surfaces: the absorb pass grows
  small accidental analytic fits (6-face cylinder ribbons on the saddle)
  with exactly-on-surface neighbors, hiding them from region gathering.
  Absorption/refinement run after, with B-spline surfaces excluded as
  targets (the fit doesn't vouch for faces outside its region; chordal
  absorption extended the arch face into the surface's extrapolation zone,
  a 1.7% volume error).
- Region gathering absorbs ≤16-face selections of any type connected by
  smooth edges (≤ --angular-tolerance dihedral): freeform surfaces bait the
  analytic detectors (coplanar strip pairs at wave inflections, cylinder
  ribbons on the saddle, 9-12-face cones on the hill_with_hole bump peak).
  Guards: components with no single-face planar member are never fitted,
  and absorbed faces must not outnumber the single-face leftovers.
- Multi-face planes whose entire shared boundary with a component is
  smooth are tangent-merged (bspline_blister's exactly-planar margin is
  part of the reference's B-spline face; keeping it separate invents a
  fake feature edge).
- Grid stations sit at the boundary vertices' own pinned positions,
  subdivided to an interior-density target (~1.5·sqrt(region vertices)):
  stations between coarse-profile vertices pin the fit to the chordal
  prism (the arch's own 1.7% chordal volume deficit), while
  boundary-derived counts undersample dense interiors (an 8x8 grid on the
  946-vertex hill_with_hole).
- Interpolation before approximation: OCCT's least-squares approximator
  reports IsDone while overshooting Tol3D by millimeters near strongly
  curved patch boundaries (measured 1.8 mm on the saddle).
- Fit validation seeds each projection from the vertex's own
  parameterization value: sequential NextValueOfUV seeding breaks at mesh
  row wraps, and both it and ValueOfUV settle in wrong local minima on
  many-knot surfaces (a gap re-check now also guards every chart
  projection).
- The boundary-chain edge repair gains its planned third arm: a
  GeomAPI_PointsToBSpline curve through the chain vertices, best-of-three
  with the line and circle. First demanded by the arch's elliptical
  arch-wall junction (IntSS degenerate; the circle repair's 1 mm deviation
  cost 1.6% volume; the B-spline fits it to 1.8e-2 mm).

Results: 7 of 8 tests/nurbs models pass full --compare (volumes within
2.7e-6..5.2e-3 relative of the exact references); elliptical_cylinder
(closed periodic wall needing a seam) stays out of scope and is rejected
cleanly at parameterization. Full suite green (476 tests) including the
previously-passing 52 analytic models; new stage-2.7 integration tests
cover the arch, the wave (over-segmentation trap), and a chamfered cube
(must remain untouched). --stage=2.7 is now addressable; absorb's loose
rule requires targets with >2 faces so freeform strips stop dissolving
into orphan-to-orphan chains.

---
Generated with assistance from Claude Fable 5 (Anthropic, 2026)

User prompt(s):
- "Implement phase 2.7 NURBS."

```

brepper converts STL meshes to parametric STEP (branch `experiment-fable`). As of end of 2026-07-10 session:

- **Stage 2.7 NURBS fallback SHIPPED 2026-07-10 (src/stage2/bspline.rs; DEVELOPMENT_PLAN §2.7 documents the as-built algorithm).** 7 of 8 tests/nurbs models pass full `--compare` (volumes 2.7e-6…5.2e-3 relative); `elliptical_cylinder` (closed periodic wall needing a seam) is the documented out-of-scope case, rejected cleanly at parameterization (<50% grid coverage). Suite: 476 tests green (~3.5 min), clippy clean. Pipeline: Floater mean-value flattening (outer loop chord-pinned to unit square, corners at outside-selection transitions, holes float) → grid resample through the flattened triangulation → `GeomAPI_PointsToBSplineSurface` (Interpolate first, approx tol/8 then tol/2 fallback, station caps 121/181/241) → per-vertex validation. `BSplineHypothesis` owns the fitted surface + RefCell'd `ShapeAnalysis_Surface` projector; stage 3 charts wrap the SAME object (`to_handle_surface()` mints handles). Stage-2 order is now: select → refine → **2.7** → absorb → prune.
- **§2.7 design rules (each earned by a measured model failure — don't undo):** (1) 2.7 runs BEFORE absorb — absorb legitimately grows accidental analytic fits with exactly-on-surface neighbors, hiding them from gathering (saddle). (2) Gathering absorbs ≤16-face selections of ANY type across smooth edges (≤1× angular tolerance dihedral; 2× let 45° chamfers glue whole cubes into one component + fit_plane NaN'd on the closed region → "planar to 0.0"); guards: component must contain ≥1 single-face planar, absorbed ≤ singles count. (3) Tangent-plane merge: multi-face plane whose ENTIRE component boundary is smooth joins the region (blister margin = part of reference B-spline face). (4) B-splines are never absorb/refine TARGETS (fit doesn't vouch beyond its region; OCCT surfaces extrapolate — cost arch 1.7% volume). (5) Grid stations AT boundary-vertex pinned positions, subdivided to ~1.5·√(n_verts) interior target: mid-chord stations pin the fit to the chordal prism (arch's mesh is itself 1.7% low on volume!); boundary-count grids undersample dense interiors (8×8 on 946-vert hill_with_hole); vertex-u quantiles produce near-duplicate stations → singular interpolation → f64::MAX garbage.
- **OCCT gotchas from §2.7:** `GeomAPI_PointsToBSplineSurface` approximation reports IsDone while overshooting Tol3D by MILLIMETERS near strongly curved patch boundaries (saddle: 1.8mm) — interpolation is trustworthy, approximation is not. `NextValueOfUV` Newton settles in nearby local minima below its maxpreci fallback (bogus 1.4mm gaps on on-surface points) and `ValueOfUV`'s global search is too coarse on many-knot surfaces — every projection needs a gap re-check (PROJ_GAP_RECHECK=0.02mm, fresh ValueOfUV, keep better), and validation must seed each vertex from its OWN Floater UV (sequential seeding breaks at mesh row wraps). Floater bijectivity needs the solve converged (GS delta <1e-10 enforced; ~1k iters typical) and mean-value squeezes corner triangles into slivers — point location needs a clamp-to-nearest-triangle fallback within 1 bin or hole-fill membranes poison the grid.
- Stage 3.3 chain repair now has the B-spline third arm (`GeomAPI_PointsToBSpline` through chain vertices, best-of-{keep,circle,bspline} by chain deviation, open chains only) — first demanded by arch's elliptical junction (IntSS degenerate on ONE of two symmetric edges; circle repair cost 1.6% volume). Corner refinement skips B-spline-adjacent corners (mesh vertex beats the ~1e-2 fit). absorb's loose ≤2-face rule now requires target >2 faces (freeform strips were dissolving orphan-to-orphan). Stage numbering: code labels selection "2.6", `--stage=2.7` = NURBS, Stage::last_minor(2)=7.
- Known residual quirks: bspline_hill/hill_with_hole volumes sit at ~5e-3/4e-3 (fit-vs-exact-reference, inside the 1% gate); stage 2.2/2.5 analytic BFS dominates runtime on dense freeform meshes (~50-60s for gridded 3k-face models — cylinder/torus seeding, NOT §2.7 which is <1s strips / ~10s gridded). tests/stage2_integration.rs has 3 nurbs tests (arch, wave, chamfered-cube-untouched; all fast).
- **--compare is strict**: >1% volume mismatch and unreadable written STEP are hard errors; `-o /dev/null` is incompatible with `--compare` (run_test_table.sh writes a temp file).
- Test models: tests/nurbs/ = 8 exact-reference pairs (gen-test-models; strip meshes for ruled surfaces by user decision — 2-ring sampling along rulings; references are EXACT OCCT geometry, never fitted). BRepGProp quadrature untrustworthy on freeform faces (fixed Gauss ~0.5% low on bumps; adaptive 4% high on boolean-trimmed sheets) — generator validates against mesh volume. The installed ccad segfaults, tests/ccad/generated can't be regenerated.
- Tests must assert on stage 2.6 *selected* surfaces, never raw hypothesis counts. AGENTS.md defines commit format (model name + user prompts, `git commit -F tmp/COMMITMSG`); `cargo clippy` (default targets) is the clean gate.
- Debugging stage 2.7: `-vv` prints per-component composition (singles/absorbed), region loops, side counts, corners, per-attempt failures; `-vvv` adds mean-value solve stats, outer-loop 3D samples, fit-residual-vs-own-grid probe (separates fit failure from sampler/projection failure — the decisive tool this session), and a fold detector (sampler at a failing vertex's own UV must return that vertex).

## 🤖 Assistant
<!-- msg_011CcuKRJHEcK9SHfEicQLeC -->

Everything I need is confirmed. Here's the assessment.

## What making elliptical_cylinder pass would require

**The model and today's failure.** The reference is a prism of an exact `gp_Elips` (12×7, 18 tall): the STEP contains one `SURFACE_OF_LINEAR_EXTRUSION` wall face — a **closed periodic surface with a seam edge** — plus two planar caps bounded by ellipse edges. The mesh wall arrives as 92 full-height strips. Stage 2.7 gathers the wall region correctly, but Floater parameterization needs disk topology and the wall is an annulus (two boundary rings, no outer disk boundary): one ring gets pinned to the square, the free ring collapses inward, grid coverage drops below 50%, and the region is rejected cleanly. The wall then reconstructs as ~92 planar facets whose junction edges/vertices correspond to nothing in the reference, so stage 3.1 compare hard-errors.

**Why there's no shortcut.** Splitting the wall into two open B-spline patches (cut at two azimuths) would avoid all seam machinery — and can't pass: the two vertical junctions would be fake edges, and the 3.1 edge compare measures their mesh chains against reference edges (the nearest ones are the cap ellipses, many mm away mid-wall). The compare semantics force exactly one periodic face, matching the reference. This is the same lesson the blister taught about invented edges.

**Work package A — stage 2.7, fitting a periodic surface.** This is the smaller half:

1. *Detect closed-band topology*: Euler characteristic V−E+F = 0 with two boundary loops (the arch scores 1; the strip wall: 184−276+92 = 0). Both loops and the counts are already computed in `build_region`.
2. *Cut a seam for parameterization*: pick a full-height mesh edge path (on a strip mesh any shared strip edge runs bottom ring → top ring directly), duplicate its vertices, pin **both** rings by cumulative chord fraction with the seam copies at u=0 and u=1, and reuse the existing mean-value solve on the resulting disk (strip meshes have no interior vertices at all).
3. *Fit periodically*: the binding exists — `PointsToBSplineSurface::interpolate_array2ofpnt_parametrizationtype_bool(..., thePeriodic=true)`, and the OCCT doc in the bindings confirms the convention: periodic **along U, the first array index, using the first row as the periodic boundary** — so the grid omits the duplicate closing column. Validation machinery works as-is (the projector handles periodic surfaces; seeds just need mod-period care).

**Work package B — stage 3, the wrapped B-spline face.** This is the riskier half. My B-spline chart currently hard-codes `u_periodic() = false`, which is what disables all seam/winding machinery:

1. *The period problem*: the whole stage-3.4 unwrap/winding/seam apparatus hard-codes 2π as the period (`TWO_PI` in `sample_edge_uv`, loop alignment, pcurve shifts). The cheap, safe path is to **rescale the fitted surface's U knots to [0, 2π]** — an exact reparameterization, and `Geom_BSplineSurface::set_u_knots` and `set_u_periodic` are both bound. Then every existing 2π mechanism applies unchanged, and the chart just reports `u_periodic() = true`. The alternative — threading a `u_period` value through all that validated math — is a much bigger refactor I'd avoid.
2. *Seam anchors*: `plan_seam_anchors` needs a vertex pair at matching azimuths on both rings. Extrusion strip meshes have them (the rings are translates of each other); irregular closed walls generally don't and would hit the already-documented "edge splitting" hard error — acceptable, same as analytic surfaces today. The seam edge itself is a `u_iso` of the fitted surface (verified working on B-splines) through the existing `make_seam_edge` path.
3. *Cap junction edges*: two closed-loop ReconEdges (ellipses). If `IntSS(plane, periodic B-spline)` returns them degenerate, the closed-loop chain rescue currently offers only a circle — wrong for an ellipse (the exact failure that cost the arch 1.6% volume on an open chain). That means the **periodic chain-repair arm**: `GeomAPI_Interpolate` with its periodic flag, which is bound.
4. *Gauge freedom helps*: our seam azimuth need not match the reference's. This model creates no 3.1 BRepVertices (nowhere do 3+ surfaces meet), seam vertices exist only as 3.4 anchors, and volume/face-distance/round-trip are gauge-invariant — the same insight as the sphere-axis gauge choice that killed the pole special cases.

**Risks and estimate.** The genuinely uncertain parts: the periodic-Interpolate conventions deserve a small standalone experiment; `set_u_knots` on a periodic surface has fussy knot-array requirements (fallback: rebuild via the explicit periodic constructor, binding to be verified); and the seeded projector's branch behavior near the seam (principal u flips between ~0 and ~2π) is exactly what the analytic unwrap handles but is the numerically delicate spot. Package A is roughly a day; package B is a few days *if* the knot-rescale trick works, dominated by 3.4 debugging (the `--stage=3.4 -v` pcurve-deviation dumps exist for that). Beyond the test itself, closed freeform walls (swept blends) are common in real exports, so the periodic path has value toward the README goal — TODO.md now carries this as the named follow-up with these two entry points.

One status note: the §2.7 implementation, tests, and doc updates from this session are complete and verified (suite green, RESULTS.md regenerated at 59/65 with only elliptical_cylinder as the non-bad failure) but sit uncommitted — the prepared message is in tmp/COMMITMSG, and committing was the next step when this question came in.

## 🤖 Assistant
<!-- msg_011CcuX34NrfsXWxEZ8gySz2 -->

Confirmed — the 3.4 face-count comparison is informational only. So here's the full picture.

## Short answer

It helps a lot: it deletes the riskiest, most uncertain half of the work — the periodic/seam machinery in stage 3.4 — and converts the job from "generalize validated 2π-hard-coded topology code" (3–5 days, one genuinely open-ended unknown) into mostly bookkeeping (~1.5–2 days, one contained numerical hazard). But it must relax slightly more than the edge compare, and it buys a non-canonical output topology.

## The design it unlocks

The trick is that the relaxed compare permits **two faces sharing one fitted surface**, which sidesteps everything periodic:

1. **Fit stays almost identical to the open-patch path.** Annulus detection (Euler characteristic V−E+F = 0; the strip wall scores exactly 0, a disk 1) and the seam-cut parameterization are needed regardless. But the fit becomes an *ordinary non-periodic* `Interpolate` with the seam column duplicated at u=0 and u=1. A nice property of clamped tensor-product interpolation: the first and last pole columns equal the shared data column, so the two boundary iso-curves are *identical* — the wall closes exactly (C0; a tiny tangent crease at the closure, well under tolerance). No periodic-Interpolate experiment, no knot rescaling.

2. **Two hypotheses, one surface object.** Split the region at two vertex-aligned cut paths (cut 1 = the parameter origin, cut 2 ≈ half-way) into two `BSplineHypothesis` entries holding handles to the same `Geom_BSplineSurface` — the same refcounted-handle pattern `create_occt_surface` already uses. Each face is then a plain UV rectangle: `u_periodic()` stays false, and **all** of the seam/winding/composite-wire/`plan_seam_anchors` machinery — plus the TWO_PI-period generalization that was the big unknown — stays untouched.

3. **The junction edges come almost free.** Tangency detection classifies the two cut edges tangent (identical normals — same surface), which routes them to the chain machinery; for an extrusion the cut path is a straight ruling, so the existing line fit is exact, and the B-spline chain arm covers curved cuts. Better still, the cap junctions become *open arcs* with endpoint vertices instead of closed loops — so the periodic chain-repair arm (`GeomAPI_Interpolate`) I listed as probable work is no longer needed either.

## What must actually be relaxed

"Allow a seam" needs to be slightly wider than the edge check, and it should be tag-based, not tolerance-based:

- **3.1 edge check**: the two cut edges' mesh chains lie mid-wall, many mm from any reference edge — no tolerance fixes that; they must be exempted. Since stage 2.7 *creates* the split, it can tag those ReconEdges explicitly ("same-surface cut"), and the compare exempts exactly the tagged edges.
- **3.1 vertex check**: the split creates 4 corner vertices (cap + wall-A + wall-B meet) with no reference counterparts — same tagging, same exemption. This is the part your framing didn't mention but is equally load-bearing.
- Nothing else: the 3.4 face count is informational, and face-sample distance, orientation, shells, volume, and round-trip are all gauge-invariant.

The tagging discipline matters. The 3.1 edge check is precisely what caught every over-segmentation failure this session (blister's fake rim edge, hill_with_hole's cone patches), and the repo's history has a standing lesson about softened compares (the warning-only volume check that let a 46% regression sail through). A narrow "edges we deliberately manufactured" exemption keeps the check sharp; a general relaxation would not.

## Remaining risk and the honest costs

The one real numerical hazard left: the surface self-touches along the closure, so a point there projects ambiguously to u≈0 or u≈1. The seeded `NextValueOfUV` chain handles it once each face's chart is primed from its own interior (the gap re-check won't help here — both branches have gap ≈ 0), so it needs one deliberate seed-priming line and a test.

Costs: the STEP contains a wall split into two faces with two artificial edges — valid B-rep, fine for consumers, but not what CAD kernels emit (they write one periodic face with a seam, which is exactly what the reference is). And it defers rather than builds the periodic machinery that real-world closed blends will eventually demand — though the reusable 80% (annulus detection, cut parameterization) is shared, so the periodic path can be layered on later with the split as a permanent fallback.

My take: as a permanent design it's a compromise on the project's "CAD-idiomatic output" goal, but as a staged plan it's attractive — land the split-with-tagged-exemptions version cheaply, keep elliptical_cylinder's scoreboard entry honest by marking it "passes with seam-split relaxation," and treat the periodic face as the follow-up that removes the exemption.

/// A connected freeform region: faces, triangulated geometry, and ordered
/// boundary loops (region on the left of each directed boundary edge, i.e.
/// counter-clockwise seen from outside the solid).
struct Region {
    faces: Vec<usize>,
    /// Region triangulation (quads split along the v0–v2 diagonal), global
    /// vertex indices, mesh winding preserved.
    tris: Vec<[usize; 3]>,
    /// Sorted unique global vertex indices.
    verts: Vec<usize>,
    /// Global → local vertex index.
    local: HashMap<usize, usize>,
    /// Boundary loops as ordered (vertex, outside_surface_id) pairs: the
    /// directed boundary edge starts at `vertex` and is shared with a face
    /// of selected surface `outside_surface_id`.
    loops: Vec<Vec<(usize, usize)>>,
}

fn build_region(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    faces: Vec<usize>,
    face_to_selected: &[usize],
    in_region: &[bool],
) -> Result<Region, String> {
    let mut tris = Vec::with_capacity(faces.len() * 2);
    let mut vert_set = HashSet::new();
    // Directed boundary edges: (a → b, outside surface id).
    let mut boundary_next: HashMap<usize, Vec<(usize, usize)>> = HashMap::new();
    let mut n_boundary_edges = 0usize;

    for &fi in &faces {
        let face = &mesh.faces[fi];
        let vc = face.vertex_count as usize;
        let vi = &face.vertex_indices;
        for &v in &vi[..vc] {
            vert_set.insert(v);
        }
        tris.push([vi[0], vi[1], vi[2]]);
        if vc == 4 {
            tris.push([vi[0], vi[2], vi[3]]);
        }
        for k in 0..vc {
            let ni = face.neighbors[k];
            let outside = ni >= 0 && !in_region[ni as usize];
            if ni < 0 || outside {
                let a = vi[k];
                let b = vi[(k + 1) % vc];
                let outside_id = if ni >= 0 {
                    face_to_selected[ni as usize]
                } else {
                    usize::MAX
                };
                boundary_next.entry(a).or_default().push((b, outside_id));
                n_boundary_edges += 1;
            }
        }
    }

    // Chain directed boundary edges into loops. Start each loop at its
    // smallest unconsumed vertex for determinism.
    let mut loops = Vec::new();
    let mut consumed = 0usize;
    while consumed < n_boundary_edges {
        let start = *boundary_next
            .iter()
            .filter(|(_, outs)| !outs.is_empty())
            .map(|(a, _)| a)
            .min()
            .ok_or("boundary chaining lost edges")?;
        let mut lp: Vec<(usize, usize)> = Vec::new();
        let mut cur = start;
        loop {
            let outs = boundary_next
                .get_mut(&cur)
                .filter(|o| !o.is_empty())
                .ok_or_else(|| format!("open boundary chain at vertex {cur}"))?;
            // A vertex can have two outgoing boundary edges when the region
            // touches itself at a vertex; taking any unconsumed edge still
            // partitions the boundary into valid loops.
            let (next, outside_id) = outs.swap_remove(0);
            lp.push((cur, outside_id));
            consumed += 1;
            cur = next;
            if cur == start {
                break;
            }
            if lp.len() > n_boundary_edges {
                return Err("boundary chaining did not close".to_string());
            }
        }
        if lp.len() >= 3 {
            loops.push(lp);
        }
    }
    if loops.is_empty() {
        return Err("region has no boundary loop".to_string());
    }

    let mut verts: Vec<usize> = vert_set.into_iter().collect();
    verts.sort_unstable();
    let local: HashMap<usize, usize> =
        verts.iter().enumerate().map(|(li, &vi)| (vi, li)).collect();

    Ok(Region { faces, tris, verts, local, loops })
}

/// Index (into `loops`) of the outer boundary loop: the one with the largest
/// 3D bounding-box diagonal. Other loops are holes and float freely in the
/// parameterization.
fn outer_loop_index(region: &Region, vertices: &[MeshVertex]) -> usize {
    let mut best = 0;
    let mut best_diag = -1.0;
    for (li, lp) in region.loops.iter().enumerate() {
        let mut lo = [f64::INFINITY; 3];
        let mut hi = [f64::NEG_INFINITY; 3];
        for &(vi, _) in lp {
            let v = &vertices[vi];
            for (d, val) in [v.x, v.y, v.z].iter().enumerate() {
                lo[d] = lo[d].min(*val);
                hi[d] = hi[d].max(*val);
            }
        }
        let diag = (0..3).map(|d| (hi[d] - lo[d]).powi(2)).sum::<f64>();
        if diag > best_diag {
            best_diag = diag;
            best = li;
        }
    }
    best
}
