/// Sentinel "outside selection" id for boundary edges created by a seam
/// cut: they were interior mesh edges, so no outside selection exists. A
/// distinct value from usize::MAX (open mesh boundary) so corner detection
/// sees transitions exactly at the cut endpoints.
const CUT_OUTSIDE: usize = usize::MAX - 1;

/// A connected freeform region: faces, triangulated geometry, and ordered
/// boundary loops (region on the left of each directed boundary edge, i.e.
/// counter-clockwise seen from outside the solid). Vertices are indexed
/// LOCALLY: a seam cut duplicates the cut-path vertices, so one global mesh
/// vertex can appear as two local vertices.
struct Region {
    faces: Vec<usize>,
    /// Region triangulation (quads split along the v0–v2 diagonal), local
    /// vertex indices, mesh winding preserved.
    tris: Vec<[usize; 3]>,
    /// Region face index (into `faces`) of each triangle.
    tri_face: Vec<usize>,
    /// Local → global mesh vertex index (seam-cut clones repeat one).
    verts: Vec<usize>,
    /// Local vertex positions (clones repeat their original's).
    positions: Vec<[f64; 3]>,
    /// Global → one local index (originals win over clones), for seeding.
    global_to_local: HashMap<usize, usize>,
    /// Outside selection id per undirected GLOBAL vertex pair of the
    /// original region boundary (global keys are clone-transparent).
    outside: HashMap<(usize, usize), usize>,
    /// Boundary loops as ordered (local vertex, outside_surface_id) pairs:
    /// the directed boundary edge starts at `vertex` and is shared with a
    /// face of selected surface `outside_surface_id` (or CUT_OUTSIDE).
    loops: Vec<Vec<(usize, usize)>>,
}

fn build_region(
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    faces: Vec<usize>,
    face_to_selected: &[usize],
    in_region: &[bool],
) -> Result<Region, String> {
    let mut vert_set = HashSet::new();
    for &fi in &faces {
        let face = &mesh.faces[fi];
        for &v in &face.vertex_indices[..face.vertex_count as usize] {
            vert_set.insert(v);
        }
    }
    let mut verts: Vec<usize> = vert_set.into_iter().collect();
    verts.sort_unstable();
    let global_to_local: HashMap<usize, usize> =
        verts.iter().enumerate().map(|(li, &vi)| (vi, li)).collect();
    let positions: Vec<[f64; 3]> = verts
        .iter()
        .map(|&vi| {
            let v = &mesh.vertices[vi];
            [v.x, v.y, v.z]
        })
        .collect();

    let mut tris = Vec::with_capacity(faces.len() * 2);
    let mut tri_face = Vec::with_capacity(faces.len() * 2);
    let mut outside: HashMap<(usize, usize), usize> = HashMap::new();
    for (rf, &fi) in faces.iter().enumerate() {
        let face = &mesh.faces[fi];
        let vc = face.vertex_count as usize;
        let vi = &face.vertex_indices;
        let l = |g: usize| global_to_local[&g];
        tris.push([l(vi[0]), l(vi[1]), l(vi[2])]);
        tri_face.push(rf);
        if vc == 4 {
            tris.push([l(vi[0]), l(vi[2]), l(vi[3])]);
            tri_face.push(rf);
        }
        for k in 0..vc {
            let ni = face.neighbors[k];
            if ni < 0 || !in_region[ni as usize] {
                let a = vi[k];
                let b = vi[(k + 1) % vc];
                let outside_id = if ni >= 0 {
                    face_to_selected[ni as usize]
                } else {
                    usize::MAX
                };
                outside.insert((a.min(b), a.max(b)), outside_id);
            }
        }
    }

    let mut region = Region {
        faces,
        tris,
        tri_face,
        verts,
        positions,
        global_to_local,
        outside,
        loops: Vec::new(),
    };
    region.loops = chain_boundary_loops(&region)?;
    if region.loops.is_empty() {
        return Err("region has no boundary loop".to_string());
    }
    Ok(region)
}

/// Chain the triangulation's boundary edges (edges with exactly one
/// incident triangle) into ordered loops, region on the left. Outside ids
/// come from the region's global-pair map; edges absent from it are
/// seam-cut edges.
fn chain_boundary_loops(region: &Region) -> Result<Vec<Vec<(usize, usize)>>, String> {
    // Count incidences per undirected local edge; remember the directed
    // form each edge takes in its (unique, for boundary edges) triangle.
    let mut count: HashMap<(usize, usize), (u32, (usize, usize))> = HashMap::new();
    for tri in &region.tris {
        for k in 0..3 {
            let (a, b) = (tri[k], tri[(k + 1) % 3]);
            let e = count.entry((a.min(b), a.max(b))).or_insert((0, (a, b)));
            e.0 += 1;
            e.1 = (a, b);
        }
    }
    let mut boundary_next: HashMap<usize, Vec<(usize, usize)>> = HashMap::new();
    let mut n_boundary_edges = 0usize;
    for (&key, &(c, (a, b))) in &count {
        if c == 1 {
            let ga = region.verts[key.0];
            let gb = region.verts[key.1];
            let outside_id = region
                .outside
                .get(&(ga.min(gb), ga.max(gb)))
                .copied()
                .unwrap_or(CUT_OUTSIDE);
            boundary_next.entry(a).or_default().push((b, outside_id));
            n_boundary_edges += 1;
        }
    }
    // Deterministic chaining: smallest start vertex, smallest next first.
    for outs in boundary_next.values_mut() {
        outs.sort_unstable();
    }
    let mut loops = Vec::new();
    let mut consumed = 0usize;
    while consumed < n_boundary_edges {
        let start = *boundary_next
            .iter()
            .filter(|(_, outs)| !outs.is_empty())
            .map(|(a, _)| a)
            .min()
            .ok_or("boundary chaining lost edges")?;
        let mut lp: Vec<(usize, usize)> = Vec::new();
        let mut cur = start;
        loop {
            let outs = boundary_next
                .get_mut(&cur)
                .filter(|o| !o.is_empty())
                .ok_or_else(|| format!("open boundary chain at local vertex {cur}"))?;
            // A vertex can have two outgoing boundary edges when the region
            // touches itself at a vertex; taking any unconsumed edge still
            // partitions the boundary into valid loops.
            let (next, outside_id) = outs.remove(0);
            lp.push((cur, outside_id));
            consumed += 1;
            cur = next;
            if cur == start {
                break;
            }
            if lp.len() > n_boundary_edges {
                return Err("boundary chaining did not close".to_string());
            }
        }
        if lp.len() >= 3 {
            loops.push(lp);
        }
    }
    Ok(loops)
}

/// Squared bounding-box diagonal of each boundary loop.
fn loop_diags_sq(region: &Region) -> Vec<f64> {
    region
        .loops
        .iter()
        .map(|lp| {
            let mut lo = [f64::INFINITY; 3];
            let mut hi = [f64::NEG_INFINITY; 3];
            for &(li, _) in lp {
                let p = region.positions[li];
                for d in 0..3 {
                    lo[d] = lo[d].min(p[d]);
                    hi[d] = hi[d].max(p[d]);
                }
            }
            (0..3).map(|d| (hi[d] - lo[d]).powi(2)).sum::<f64>()
        })
        .collect()
}

/// Index (into `loops`) of the outer boundary loop: the one with the largest
/// 3D bounding-box diagonal. Other loops are holes and float freely in the
/// parameterization.
fn outer_loop_index(region: &Region) -> usize {
    loop_diags_sq(region)
        .iter()
        .enumerate()
        .max_by(|a, b| a.1.partial_cmp(b.1).unwrap())
        .map(|(i, _)| i)
        .unwrap_or(0)
}

/// Index (into `loops`) of the outer boundary loop: the one with the largest
/// 3D bounding-box diagonal. Other loops are holes and float freely in the
/// parameterization.
fn outer_loop_index(region: &Region) -> usize {
    loop_diags_sq(region)
        .iter()
        .enumerate()
        .max_by(|a, b| a.1.partial_cmp(b.1).unwrap())
        .map(|(i, _)| i)
        .unwrap_or(0)
}

/// True when the region is a closed band (annulus) rather than a disk with
/// holes: it has a second boundary loop of extent comparable to the largest
/// (≥ half its bounding-box diagonal). A small hole floats freely in the
/// disk parameterization; a comparable second loop means the region wraps
/// around (e.g. the wall of a closed prism) and must be seam-cut first.
fn is_closed_band(region: &Region) -> bool {
    let mut d = loop_diags_sq(region);
    if d.len() < 2 {
        return false;
    }
    d.sort_by(|a, b| b.partial_cmp(a).unwrap());
    d[1] >= 0.25 * d[0]
}

/// Cut a closed-band region into a disk along a shortest vertex path
/// between its two largest boundary loops. The path vertices are
/// duplicated: triangles on the path's right side (region winding) switch
/// to the clones, and the boundary is re-chained — the two loops merge
/// into one, with the two cut copies flagged CUT_OUTSIDE. Clones keep
/// their original's global index and position, so the sampled seam columns
/// at the parameter extremes carry identical 3D data and the fitted
/// surface closes exactly.
fn cut_region_seam(mut region: Region, verbosity: u8) -> Result<Region, String> {
    // The two largest loops.
    let diags = loop_diags_sq(&region);
    let mut order: Vec<usize> = (0..diags.len()).collect();
    order.sort_by(|&a, &b| diags[b].partial_cmp(&diags[a]).unwrap());
    let (la, lb) = (order[0], order[1]);
    let on_a: HashSet<usize> = region.loops[la].iter().map(|&(li, _)| li).collect();
    let on_b: HashSet<usize> = region.loops[lb].iter().map(|&(li, _)| li).collect();

    // Vertex adjacency over the triangulation.
    let nv = region.verts.len();
    let mut adj: Vec<Vec<usize>> = vec![Vec::new(); nv];
    for tri in &region.tris {
        for k in 0..3 {
            let (a, b) = (tri[k], tri[(k + 1) % 3]);
            adj[a].push(b);
            adj[b].push(a);
        }
    }
    for l in adj.iter_mut() {
        l.sort_unstable();
        l.dedup();
    }

    // Multi-source BFS (hop count) from loop A to loop B; deterministic
    // frontier order.
    let mut parent = vec![usize::MAX; nv];
    let mut seen = vec![false; nv];
    let mut frontier: Vec<usize> = {
        let mut f: Vec<usize> = on_a.iter().copied().collect();
        f.sort_unstable();
        f
    };
    for &s in &frontier {
        seen[s] = true;
    }
    let mut hit = None;
    'bfs: while !frontier.is_empty() {
        let mut next = Vec::new();
        for &v in &frontier {
            for &w in &adj[v] {
                if !seen[w] {
                    seen[w] = true;
                    parent[w] = v;
                    if on_b.contains(&w) {
                        hit = Some(w);
                        break 'bfs;
                    }
                    next.push(w);
                }
            }
        }
        frontier = next;
    }
    let Some(end) = hit else {
        return Err("closed band: no path between boundary loops".to_string());
    };
    let mut path = vec![end];
    while parent[*path.last().unwrap()] != usize::MAX {
        path.push(parent[*path.last().unwrap()]);
    }
    path.reverse(); // loop A → loop B
    if verbosity >= 2 {
        eprintln!(
            "  Stage 2.7: closed band — seam cut along {} vertices from \
             [{:.3},{:.3},{:.3}] to [{:.3},{:.3},{:.3}]",
            path.len(),
            region.positions[path[0]][0],
            region.positions[path[0]][1],
            region.positions[path[0]][2],
            region.positions[path[path.len() - 1]][0],
            region.positions[path[path.len() - 1]][1],
            region.positions[path[path.len() - 1]][2],
        );
    }

    // Classify the triangles flanking each path edge: with consistent mesh
    // winding, the triangle whose winding contains pi→pi+1 is on the LEFT
    // of the directed path; the one containing pi+1→pi is on the RIGHT.
    // Right-side fans switch to the clones.
    let path_edge: HashSet<(usize, usize)> = path
        .windows(2)
        .map(|w| (w[0].min(w[1]), w[0].max(w[1])))
        .collect();
    let mut right_seed: HashMap<usize, Vec<usize>> = HashMap::new(); // path vtx → tri ids
    for (ti, tri) in region.tris.iter().enumerate() {
        for k in 0..3 {
            let (a, b) = (tri[k], tri[(k + 1) % 3]);
            if path_edge.contains(&(a.min(b), a.max(b))) {
                // Directed path order: does (a, b) match path direction?
                let pa = path.iter().position(|&p| p == a).unwrap();
                let along = pa + 1 < path.len() && path[pa + 1] == b;
                if !along {
                    // Contains the reversed edge → right side.
                    right_seed.entry(a).or_default().push(ti);
                    right_seed.entry(b).or_default().push(ti);
                }
            }
        }
    }

    // Per path vertex: flood its star from the right-side seeds without
    // crossing path edges; those triangles get the clone.
    let mut vert_tris: Vec<Vec<usize>> = vec![Vec::new(); nv];
    for (ti, tri) in region.tris.iter().enumerate() {
        for &v in tri {
            vert_tris[v].push(ti);
        }
    }
    for (pi, &pv) in path.iter().enumerate() {
        let clone = region.verts.len();
        region.verts.push(region.verts[pv]);
        region.positions.push(region.positions[pv]);

        let star: Vec<usize> = vert_tris[pv].clone();
        let seeds: Vec<usize> = right_seed.get(&pv).cloned().unwrap_or_default();
        if seeds.is_empty() {
            return Err(format!("seam cut: path vertex {pi} has no right-side triangle"));
        }
        // Star adjacency: two star triangles are connected iff they share
        // an edge incident to pv that is not a path edge.
        let mut in_right: HashSet<usize> = seeds.iter().copied().collect();
        let mut stack = seeds;
        while let Some(ti) = stack.pop() {
            let tri = region.tris[ti];
            for k in 0..3 {
                let (a, b) = (tri[k], tri[(k + 1) % 3]);
                if a != pv && b != pv {
                    continue; // not incident to pv
                }
                let key = (a.min(b), a.max(b));
                if path_edge.contains(&key) {
                    continue; // never cross the cut
                }
                for &tj in &vert_tris[pv] {
                    if tj != ti && !in_right.contains(&tj) {
                        let tjt = region.tris[tj];
                        let has_edge = (0..3).any(|m| {
                            let (c, d) = (tjt[m], tjt[(m + 1) % 3]);
                            (c.min(d), c.max(d)) == key
                        });
                        if has_edge {
                            in_right.insert(tj);
                            stack.push(tj);
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        if in_right.len() >= star.len() {
            return Err(format!(
                "seam cut: path vertex {pi} star did not split ({} of {} triangles on the right)",
                in_right.len(),
                star.len(),
            ));
        }
        for &ti in &in_right {
            for v in region.tris[ti].iter_mut() {
                if *v == pv {
                    *v = clone;
                }
            }
            vert_tris[clone].push(ti);
        }
        vert_tris[pv].retain(|ti| !in_right.contains(ti));
    }

    region.loops = chain_boundary_loops(&region)?;
    if region.loops.len() != diags.len() - 1 {
        return Err(format!(
            "seam cut did not merge the loops ({} before, {} after)",
            diags.len(),
            region.loops.len(),
        ));
    }
    Ok(region)
}

## 🤖💭 Assistant
<!-- msg_011Cd3xQLiPoq1mmY4NHwaRL -->

> I'm spotting a bug in how the right_seed classification handles path edges — when checking if vertex `a` appears in the path, I'm finding its position, but if the triangle edge is oriented opposite to the path direction (like the path goes b→a but the edge is stored as a→b), the logic incorrectly classifies it as being on the right side instead of along the path.
> 
> The core issue is that after rewriting triangles for previous path vertices, some of those triangles now reference cloned vertices instead of the originals, which could break the path_edge checks that rely on the original vertex pairs.
> 
> But actually, this is safe: when a right-side triangle gets rewritten and its reference to p_{i-1} becomes a reference to clone_{i-1}, that edge (pv, clone_{i-1}) only connects to other right-side triangles that were also rewritten in the same way. The original (pv, p_{i-1}) edge is now only flanked by left-side triangles, so the flood from the right side can't cross it. The blocked-edge logic still holds because the right-seed triangles found via reversed path edges still contain pv, even after their vertices get rewritten.
> 
> For endpoint path vertices on the boundary rings, their star is a half-disk and the flood stops at both the path edge and the boundary automatically. The right seeds exist from that single path edge's right triangle. There's also a potential edge case with the `in_right.len() >= star.len()` guard when the path edge doesn't actually split the star.
> 
> Path edges are interior by construction since they connect two loops through the region, but I need to check if a path edge could lie on a hole's boundary — if it does, that edge would have only one flanking triangle, making right_seed potentially empty, which I handle gracefully. Now I'm going through the remaining callers to update them, starting with `choose_cor`.
> 
> I need to refactor several functions to use positions directly from the region instead of passing vertices separately: `choose_corners` takes positions as a slice, `map_outer_loop_to_square` extracts positions from the region, `solve_interior_uv` uses region.positions with local triangle indices, `UvSampler::new` drops the vertices parameter and uses region.positions for barycentric calculations, and in `fit_component` I'm removing the mesh.vertices dependency and updating all the local references accordingly.

783	/// Solve for interior (and hole-boundary) vertex UVs with mean-value
784	/// weights: each unknown vertex is the convex combination of its neighbors,
785	/// w_ij = Σ tan(γ/2)/|p_i − p_j| over the triangles flanking edge (i,j).
786	/// Plain Gauss–Seidel; the systems here are at most a few thousand unknowns.
787	fn solve_interior_uv(
788	    region: &Region,
789	    vertices: &[MeshVertex],
790	    pinned: &[bool],
791	    uv: &mut [(f64, f64)],
792	    verbosity: u8,
793	) -> Result<(), String> {
794	    let nv = region.verts.len();
795	    // Accumulate weights in BTreeMaps for deterministic iteration order.
796	    let mut weights: Vec<BTreeMap<usize, f64>> = vec![BTreeMap::new(); nv];
797	    let pos = |vi: usize| {
798	        let v = &vertices[vi];
799	        [v.x, v.y, v.z]
800	    };
801	    for tri in &region.tris {
802	        for k in 0..3 {
803	            let i = region.local[&tri[k]];
804	            if pinned[i] {
805	                continue;
806	            }
807	            let pi = pos(tri[k]);
808	            let pa = pos(tri[(k + 1) % 3]);
809	            let pb = pos(tri[(k + 2) % 3]);
810	            let ea = [pa[0] - pi[0], pa[1] - pi[1], pa[2] - pi[2]];
811	            let eb = [pb[0] - pi[0], pb[1] - pi[1], pb[2] - pi[2]];
812	            let la = (ea[0] * ea[0] + ea[1] * ea[1] + ea[2] * ea[2]).sqrt();
813	            let lb = (eb[0] * eb[0] + eb[1] * eb[1] + eb[2] * eb[2]).sqrt();
814	            if la < 1e-30 || lb < 1e-30 {
815	                return Err("degenerate triangle in region".to_string());
816	            }
817	            let cosg = ((ea[0] * eb[0] + ea[1] * eb[1] + ea[2] * eb[2]) / (la * lb))
818	                .clamp(-1.0, 1.0);
819	            let sing = (1.0 - cosg * cosg).sqrt();
820	            // tan(γ/2), stable form; clamp near-degenerate angles.
821	            let tan_half = if 1.0 + cosg < 1e-12 { 1e6 } else { sing / (1.0 + cosg) };
822	            let a = region.local[&tri[(k + 1) % 3]];
823	            let b = region.local[&tri[(k + 2) % 3]];
824	            *weights[i].entry(a).or_insert(0.0) += tan_half / la;
825	            *weights[i].entry(b).or_insert(0.0) += tan_half / lb;
826	        }
827	    }
828	
829	    let unknowns: Vec<usize> = (0..nv).filter(|&i| !pinned[i]).collect();
830	    if unknowns.is_empty() {
831	        return Ok(());
832	    }
833	    for &i in &unknowns {
834	        if weights[i].is_empty() {
835	            return Err("isolated interior vertex in region".to_string());
836	        }
837	        // Start unknowns at the square center.
838	        uv[i] = (0.5, 0.5);
839	    }
840	    let mut max_delta = f64::INFINITY;
841	    let mut iters = 0usize;
842	    for _iter in 0..30_000 {
843	        iters += 1;
844	        max_delta = 0.0;
845	        for &i in &unknowns {
846	            let mut su = 0.0;
847	            let mut sv = 0.0;
848	            let mut sw = 0.0;
849	            for (&j, &w) in &weights[i] {
850	                su += w * uv[j].0;
851	                sv += w * uv[j].1;
852	                sw += w;
853	            }
854	            let nu = su / sw;
855	            let nv2 = sv / sw;
856	            max_delta = max_delta.max((nu - uv[i].0).abs()).max((nv2 - uv[i].1).abs());
857	            uv[i] = (nu, nv2);
858	        }
859	        if max_delta < 1e-10 {
860	            break;
861	        }
862	    }
863	    if verbosity >= 3 {
864	        eprintln!(
865	            "  Stage 2.7: mean-value solve: {} unknowns, {iters} iterations, final delta {max_delta:.2e}",
866	            unknowns.len(),
867	        );
868	    }
869	    if !max_delta.is_finite() {
870	        return Err("parameterization solve diverged".to_string());
871	    }
872	    // An unconverged map silently corrupts every sample; Floater
873	    // bijectivity holds only for the exact solution.
874	    if max_delta > 1e-8 {

876	            "parameterization solve did not converge (final delta {max_delta:.2e})"
877	        ));
878	    }

/// Split the fitted hypothesis of a seam-cut closed band into two halves
/// along the around-the-band axis. Both halves share the SAME fitted
/// surface object; the caller tags them with a common
/// `shared_surface_group` so downstream code can recognize the two edges
/// between them as reconstruction artifacts (they have no counterpart in a
/// reference model, which would use one periodic face with a seam). Each
/// half spans only part of the surface's parameter range, so its two cut
/// edges are geometrically distinct and no periodic-seam machinery is
/// needed.
fn split_cut_hypothesis(
    hyp: BSplineHypothesis,
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    region: &Region,
    uv: &[(f64, f64)],
) -> Result<Vec<BSplineHypothesis>, String> {
    // The around axis runs from cut copy to cut copy: cut vertices sit at
    // that axis's parameter extremes.
    let cut_uv = region
        .loops
        .iter()
        .flatten()
        .find(|&&(_, out)| out == CUT_OUTSIDE)
        .map(|&(li, _)| uv[li])
        .ok_or("seam-cut region has no cut boundary")?;
    let around_u = cut_uv.0.min(1.0 - cut_uv.0) < cut_uv.1.min(1.0 - cut_uv.1);

    // Mean around-coordinate per region face, from its triangles.
    let mut face_sum = vec![(0.0_f64, 0usize); region.faces.len()];
    for (ti, tri) in region.tris.iter().enumerate() {
        let rf = region.tri_face[ti];
        for &li in tri {
            face_sum[rf].0 += if around_u { uv[li].0 } else { uv[li].1 };
            face_sum[rf].1 += 1;
        }
    }
    let mut faces_a = Vec::new();
    let mut faces_b = Vec::new();
    for (rf, &fi) in region.faces.iter().enumerate() {
        let mean = face_sum[rf].0 / face_sum[rf].1.max(1) as f64;
        if mean < 0.5 {
            faces_a.push(fi);
        } else {
            faces_b.push(fi);
        }
    }
    if faces_a.is_empty() || faces_b.is_empty() {
        return Err("seam split left one half empty".to_string());
    }
    let verts_of = |faces: &[usize]| -> Vec<usize> {
        let mut vs: Vec<usize> = faces
            .iter()
            .flat_map(|&fi| {
                let f = &mesh.faces[fi];
                f.vertex_indices[..f.vertex_count as usize].to_vec()
            })
            .collect();
        vs.sort_unstable();
        vs.dedup();
        vs
    };

    let surface_b = hyp
        .surface
        .to_handle_surface()
        .downcast_to_b_spline_surface()
        .ok_or("could not mint a second handle to the fitted surface")?;
    let mut hyp_b = BSplineHypothesis::new(surface_b, faces_b.clone(), verts_of(&faces_b));
    hyp_b.error_max = hyp.error_max;
    hyp_b.centroid_error_max = hyp.centroid_error_max;
    hyp_b.error_abs_sum = hyp.error_abs_sum;

    let mut hyp_a = hyp;
    hyp_a.vertices = verts_of(&faces_a);
    hyp_a.faces = faces_a;

    Ok(vec![hyp_a, hyp_b])
}"""

352	        );

The seed follows the queries within each hypothesis, though the first unseeded query on a cut-boundary point could cause branching issues.
> 
> Let me trace where the hypothesis projector gets used first in the pipeline. In `detect_tangency`, edge boundary vertices are sampled — for cut edges, the normal is computed on both hypotheses, but since the geometry is identical, the normals come out the same either way, so that's harmless. Corner refinement skips bspline-adjacent cases. The `project_point_to_selected` function is only used in corner refinement, and `vertex_distance` (for absorb/refine operations) is branch-independent. ```
/// Chart data for a B-spline face: the exact fitted surface object (shared
/// with `FaceDescriptor.surface`) and a cached ShapeAnalysis_Surface
/// projector. The projector caches internally (hence RefCell), and each
/// query is seeded from the previous solution (`NextValueOfUV`) — the
/// B-spline analog of the analytic charts' branch-continuity unwrap.
struct BSplineChartData {
    surf: OwnedPtr<geom::HandleGeomSurface>,
    sas: RefCell<OwnedPtr<shape_analysis::Surface>>,
    seed: std::cell::Cell<Option<(f64, f64)>>,
    /// Parameter bounds of the surface.
    bounds: (f64, f64, f64, f64),
    /// Parameter-space anchor inside this face's own region. The two halves
    /// of a seam-split closed band share a surface whose parameter-extreme
    /// boundary curves are the SAME 3D curve, so a projection landing on it
    /// is ambiguous between the two extremes; the branch nearer the face's
    /// own interior wins.
    home: std::cell::Cell<(f64, f64)>,
}

impl BSplineChartData {
    fn point_uv(&self, p: &[f64; 3]) -> (f64, f64) {
        use crate::stage2::bspline::{PROJ_GAP_RECHECK, PROJ_MAX_PRECISION, PROJ_PRECISION};
        let pnt = gp::Pnt::new_real3(p[0], p[1], p[2]);
        let mut sas = self.sas.borrow_mut();
        let mut best = match self.seed.get() {
            Some((su, sv)) => {
                let prev = gp::Pnt2d::new_real2(su, sv);
                let uv = sas.next_value_of_uv(&prev, &pnt, PROJ_PRECISION, PROJ_MAX_PRECISION);
                (uv.x(), uv.y(), sas.gap())
            }
            None => {
                let uv = sas.value_of_uv(&pnt, PROJ_PRECISION);
                (uv.x(), uv.y(), sas.gap())
            }
        };
        // Re-verify suspicious seeded solutions with a fresh global search:
        // NextValueOfUV's Newton step can settle in a nearby local minimum
        // without triggering its internal fallback.
        if self.seed.get().is_some() && best.2 > PROJ_GAP_RECHECK {
            let uv = sas.value_of_uv(&pnt, PROJ_PRECISION);
            let gap = sas.gap();
            if gap < best.2 {
                best = (uv.x(), uv.y(), gap);
            }
        }
        drop(sas);
        let (u, v) = self.resolve_boundary_branch(best.0, best.1);
        self.seed.set(Some((u, v)));
        (u, v)
    }

    /// A result on a parameter boundary whose opposite boundary carries the
    /// same 3D curve (a seam-split closed band) is ambiguous: keep the
    /// branch nearer this face's `home` anchor. Coincidence is verified in
    /// 3D, so ordinary (non-closed) patch boundaries are never touched.
    fn resolve_boundary_branch(&self, u: f64, v: f64) -> (f64, f64) {
        let (u0, u1, v0, v1) = self.bounds;
        let home = self.home.get();
        let mut out = (u, v);
        let eps_u = 1e-3 * (u1 - u0);
        let eps_v = 1e-3 * (v1 - v0);
        if (v - v0).abs() < eps_v || (v1 - v).abs() < eps_v {
            let here = if (v - v0).abs() < eps_v { v0 } else { v1 };
            let there = if here == v0 { v1 } else { v0 };
            let a = self.point_at(u, here);
            let b = self.point_at(u, there);
            let d2 = (a[0] - b[0]).powi(2) + (a[1] - b[1]).powi(2) + (a[2] - b[2]).powi(2);
            if d2 < 1e-12 && (there - home.1).abs() < (here - home.1).abs() {
                out.1 = there;
            }
        }
        if (u - u0).abs() < eps_u || (u1 - u).abs() < eps_u {
            let here = if (u - u0).abs() < eps_u { u0 } else { u1 };
            let there = if here == u0 { u1 } else { u0 };
            let a = self.point_at(here, out.1);
            let b = self.point_at(there, out.1);
            let d2 = (a[0] - b[0]).powi(2) + (a[1] - b[1]).powi(2) + (a[2] - b[2]).powi(2);
            if d2 < 1e-12 && (there - home.0).abs() < (here - home.0).abs() {
                out.0 = there;
            }
        }
        out
    }

    fn point_at(&self, u: f64, v: f64) -> [f64; 3] {
        let mut pnt = gp::Pnt::new_real3(0.0, 0.0, 0.0);
        self.surf.get().d0(u, v, &mut pnt);
        [pnt.x(), pnt.y(), pnt.z()]
    }
}

fn cut_region_seam(mut region: Region, verbosity: u8) -> Result<Region, String> {
    // The two largest loops.
    let diags = loop_diags_sq(&region);
    let mut order: Vec<usize> = (0..diags.len()).collect();
    order.sort_by(|&a, &b| diags[b].partial_cmp(&diags[a]).unwrap());
    let (la, lb) = (order[0], order[1]);
    let on_a: HashSet<usize> = region.loops[la].iter().map(|&(li, _)| li).collect();
    let on_b: HashSet<usize> = region.loops[lb].iter().map(|&(li, _)| li).collect();

    // Vertex adjacency over the triangulation.
    let nv = region.verts.len();
    let mut adj: Vec<Vec<usize>> = vec![Vec::new(); nv];
    for tri in &region.tris {
        for k in 0..3 {
            let (a, b) = (tri[k], tri[(k + 1) % 3]);
            adj[a].push(b);
            adj[b].push(a);
        }
    }
    for l in adj.iter_mut() {
        l.sort_unstable();
        l.dedup();
    }
```

**After:**
```
fn cut_region_seam(
    mut region: Region,
    mesh: &ConnectedMesh,
    verbosity: u8,
) -> Result<Region, String> {
    // The two largest loops.
    let diags = loop_diags_sq(&region);
    let mut order: Vec<usize> = (0..diags.len()).collect();
    order.sort_by(|&a, &b| diags[b].partial_cmp(&diags[a]).unwrap());
    let (la, lb) = (order[0], order[1]);
    let on_a: HashSet<usize> = region.loops[la].iter().map(|&(li, _)| li).collect();
    let on_b: HashSet<usize> = region.loops[lb].iter().map(|&(li, _)| li).collect();

    // Vertex adjacency over the region faces' PERIMETER edges — never quad
    // diagonals: a path along a diagonal would split that quad's two
    // triangles onto opposite sides of the cut, and the face partition
    // downstream must follow the cut exactly.
    let nv = region.verts.len();
    let mut adj: Vec<Vec<usize>> = vec![Vec::new(); nv];
    for &fi in &region.faces {
        let face = &mesh.faces[fi];
        let vc = face.vertex_count as usize;
        for k in 0..vc {
            let a = region.global_to_local[&face.vertex_indices[k]];
            let b = region.global_to_local[&face.vertex_indices[(k + 1) % vc]];
            adj[a].push(b);
            adj[b].push(a);
        }
    }
    for l in adj.iter_mut() {
        l.sort_unstable();
        l.dedup();
    }
```

409	#### 2.7 NURBS fallback (implemented 2026-07-10, \`src/stage2/bspline.rs\`)
410	
411	For groups of adjacent faces that remain as single-face planar selections after selection (i.e., they fit no analytic surface), fit a B-spline surface. Runs on the raw selection, **before** \`absorb_redundant_surfaces\`: the absorb pass legitimately grows small accidental analytic fits (cylinder ribbons on a freeform surface) with the exactly-on-surface facets around them, which would hide them from region gathering. Absorption and boundary refinement run afterwards, with B-spline surfaces excluded as targets (the fit only vouches for the faces it was built from; a chordal absorb would extend the face into the surface's extrapolation zone).
412	
413	**Algorithm (\`deduce_bspline_surfaces\`), as implemented:**
414	1. **Gather** connected components of single-face planar selections over SMOOTH mesh edges (face-normal step ≤ \`--angular-tolerance\` — a freeform surface varies by at most the tessellation's angular step between neighbors; a 45° chamfer junction is a real feature edge and must split components). The candidate set also includes selections of ≤ 16 faces of any type: freeform surfaces bait the analytic detectors locally (accidentally-coplanar strip pairs at wave inflections, 6-face cylinder ribbons carving up the saddle, 9–12-face cones on a Gaussian bump peak), and left selected they punch holes in the region and leave fake feature edges. Two guards protect real small features: a component with no single-face planar member is never fitted, and when absorbed non-single faces would outnumber the single-face leftovers the component is stripped back to the leftovers.
415	2. **Tangent-plane merge**: a multi-face planar selection whose *entire* shared boundary with a component is smooth is the flat part of the same freeform surface (B-spline local support makes exactly-planar margins — bspline_blister) and is merged in; keeping it separate invents a feature edge the reference doesn't have. Real planar neighbors (walls, bottoms) always meet freeform regions across at least some sharp edges. Analytic models are untouched — they have no ≥ 4-face freeform components.
416	3. Components below 4 faces stay single-face planar. Components planar to fitting exactness (10× vertex tolerance, NaN-guarded: the area-weighted normal of a closed region cancels to zero) become a multi-face planar hypothesis instead — a plane is preferable to a B-spline that overfits noise.
417	4. **Parameterize** the region onto the unit square: outer boundary loop pinned by cumulative chord length, 4 corners chosen where the adjacent *outside* selection changes (arc-length-quartile fallback when the boundary offers ≠ 4 transitions), interior and hole-loop vertices solved with Floater mean-value weights by Gauss–Seidel (convergence enforced — an unconverged map voids Floater's bijectivity guarantee). Quads are split along the v0–v2 diagonal for weighting and sampling.
418	5. **Resample a grid** through the flattened triangulation (uniform-bin point location; numeric misses near corner slivers are clamped to the nearest triangle within one bin — feeding them to the hole membrane extrapolates garbage). Grid stations per axis are the boundary vertices' own pinned positions (stations *between* the vertices of a coarse profile sample chord interiors and pin the fit to the chordal prism — a 1.7% volume deficit on the arch, the mesh's own chordal error), evenly subdivided up to an interior-density target of ~1.5·√(region vertices) (a flat margin tessellates coarsely: hill_with_hole has 8-vertex sides on a 946-vertex region). Genuine hole interiors are filled with a Laplacian membrane so the fitter sees smooth data. The grid is flipped if needed so d1u×d1v matches the mesh's outward normals: B-spline faces are always \`concave = false\`.
419	6. **Fit**: \`GeomAPI_PointsToBSplineSurface::Interpolate\` (chord-length, C2 cubic) first — the grid is sampled from an exact-on-surface mesh, and OCCT's least-squares approximator reports \`IsDone\` while overshooting its \`Tol3D\` by millimeters near strongly curved patch boundaries. The approximator (tol = surface/8, then surface/2) remains as fallback, and grid density retries at caps 121/181/241.
420	7. **Validate**: every region vertex and face centroid within \`--surface-tolerance\` of the fit, each projection seeded from the vertex's own parameterization value (sequential seeding breaks at mesh row wraps, and neither \`NextValueOfUV\` nor \`ValueOfUV\` recovers reliably on many-knot surfaces). On failure the component stays single-face planar with a warning.
421	
422	The \`BSplineHypothesis\` owns the fitted \`Geom_BSplineSurface\` (stage 3 reuses the same object via fresh handles) plus a cached, seed-rechecking \`ShapeAnalysis_Surface\` projector used by absorption, refinement, \`--compare\`, and stage-3 charts/normals/projections.
423

425	
426	**Implementation notes for the NURBS pass** (knowledge from the stage-3 rework, 2026-07-08; all items below are now implemented as described — kept for reference):
427	
428	- *The chart contract.* A chart provides \`point_uv(p) → (u, v, pole_radius)\` and \`point_at(u, v)\`, plus \`u_periodic()\`/\`v_periodic()\`. For a B-spline chart: \`pole_radius\` is ∞ (like the plane chart — fitted height-field patches have no UV degeneracies), and **both periodic flags must be false**. Every mod-2π unwrap/branch-lift in stage 3.4 is gated on those flags; reducing non-periodic parameter coordinates mod 2π silently corrupts them (this was a real bug on plane charts, masked for months by adaptive densification — see LEARNINGS). With both flags false, the whole seam/winding/degenerate-pole machinery self-disables and B-spline faces take the plain-loop path end to end.

```markdown
7. **Validate**: every region vertex and face centroid within `--surface-tolerance` of the fit, each projection seeded from the vertex's own parameterization value (sequential seeding breaks at mesh row wraps, and neither `NextValueOfUV` nor `ValueOfUV` recovers reliably on many-knot surfaces). On failure the component stays single-face planar with a warning.
8. **Seam-split** (closed bands only, `split_cut_hypothesis`): the validated hypothesis is split into two halves along the around-the-band axis (the axis whose parameter extremes are the cut copies), producing two `SelectedSurface::BSpline` entries that share the SAME fitted surface object and carry a common `shared_surface_group` tag. Each half spans only part of the parameter range, so its two cut edges are geometrically distinct plain edges — no periodic face, no seam edge, no winding loops. A single face would need its two coincident boundary curves to be one seam edge used twice, i.e. the full periodic machinery (below).

The `BSplineHypothesis` owns the fitted `Geom_BSplineSurface` (stage 3 reuses the same object via fresh handles) plus a cached, seed-rechecking `ShapeAnalysis_Surface` projector used by absorption, refinement, `--compare`, and stage-3 charts/normals/projections. Stage-3 charts of B-spline faces also carry a parameter-space `home` anchor (the projection of the region's mean face centroid): a projection landing on a coincident-boundary curve of a seam-split band is ambiguous between the two parameter extremes (Newton, the gap re-check, and `ValueOfUV` all cannot tell — both branches are exact), and the branch nearer the face's own interior wins. The stage 3.1 compare **exempts** edges whose two faces share a `shared_surface_group` (and the corner vertices such edge pairs meet at): they are reconstruction artifacts flagged at fit time, with no counterpart in a reference model, which represents the band as one periodic face with a seam. The exemption is tag-based, never tolerance-based — the edge compare is precisely the check that catches over-segmentation, and it stays fully armed for every edge the reconstruction did not deliberately manufacture.

**Results (2026-07-10)**: all 8 `tests/nurbs/` models pass full `--compare` (volume within 2.7e-6 … 5.2e-3 relative); `elliptical_cylinder` (closed freeform wall) passes via the seam-split reconstruction. Full 479-test suite green.

**Path to the non-compromised design (periodic B-spline face with a real seam)**: the seam-split is a deliberate compromise — the output wall is two faces plus two artificial edges where CAD kernels (and the reference) write ONE periodic face with a seam edge. Reaching that form means replacing step 8 with a periodic pipeline, and its acceptance test is precisely *removing the stage 3.1 compare exemption*:
- *Fit periodically*: `GeomAPI_PointsToBSplineSurface::Interpolate(points, ParType, thePeriodic=true)` is bound, and the binding docs state the convention: periodic **along U (the first array index), using the first row as the periodic boundary** — the closing column is omitted rather than duplicated. The cut parameterization stays as-is (it supplies the point grid); needs a small standalone experiment to confirm continuity across the closure is C2.
- *Normalize the period to 2π*: the entire stage-3.4 wrapped-face machinery (branch unwrap in `sample_edge_uv`, winding classification, pcurve shifts, seam-anchor planning) hard-codes 2π as the period. Rescaling the fitted surface's U knots to [0, 2π] is an exact reparameterization (`Geom_BSplineSurface::SetUKnots` / `SetUPeriodic` are bound) and lets every existing mechanism apply unchanged; threading a general `u_period` through that validated code is the expensive alternative.
- *Enable the periodic chart*: the B-spline chart reports `u_periodic() = true` for these faces; the analytic charts' branch-continuity unwrap then handles the seam-adjacent samples (the `home`-anchor branch resolution generalizes it).
- *Seam anchors*: `plan_seam_anchors` needs a vertex pair at matching azimuths on both rings. Extrusion strip meshes have them (the rings are translates); irregular closed walls generally do not and hit the already-documented edge-splitting future case. The seam edge itself is a `u_iso` through the existing `make_seam_edge` path.
- *Closed junction rescue*: the cap junctions become closed-loop edges again; if `IntSS` returns them degenerate, the chain repair needs its periodic arm (`GeomAPI_Interpolate` with the periodic flag — bound; the open-chain `GeomAPI_PointsToBSpline` arm cannot close a loop).
- *Keep the seam-split as fallback* for closed bands the periodic path cannot handle, and as the only option when no aligned seam-anchor pair exists without edge splitting.
```

    let stl = format!("{}/tests/nurbs/elliptical_cylinder.stl", manifest_dir());

    let groups: Vec<Option<usize>> = output
        .bspline_hypotheses
        .iter()
        .map(|h| h.shared_surface_group)
        .collect();
    assert_eq!(groups[0], groups[1], "both halves carry one group tag");
    assert!(groups[0].is_some(), "the halves must be tagged as seam-split");
}
EOF

```
Closed freeform bands reconstruct via seam-split; all 8 nurbs models pass

elliptical_cylinder — the last tests/nurbs ladder rung — needs a closed
periodic wall. Full periodic-face support means generalizing the stage-3.4
seam/winding machinery (which hard-codes a 2π period) to fitted surfaces;
instead, per discussion, closed bands are reconstructed as TWO B-spline
faces sharing ONE fitted surface, and the stage 3.1 compare exempts the
two deliberately manufactured edges between them:

- Region detection: a second boundary loop with bounding-box diagonal at
  least half the largest means the region wraps (a small hole floats
  freely in the disk parameterization; a closed prism wall cannot).
- Seam cut (cut_region_seam): shortest vertex path between the two loops
  along face PERIMETER edges only — a path along a quad's split diagonal
  tears that quad's triangles onto opposite sides of the cut (observed:
  the partition boundary jogged one vertex off the seam and the corner
  vertices landed on non-mesh positions). Path vertices are duplicated,
  right-side triangle fans (by mesh winding) switch to the clones, and
  the boundary re-chains into one loop whose cut copies carry a
  CUT_OUTSIDE id, so corner detection lands exactly at the cut endpoints.
  Region now uses local vertex indices to represent the clones.
- Fit: unchanged disk pipeline over the cut region. The clones keep their
  originals' positions, so the two parameter-extreme grid columns carry
  identical data and the clamped fit closes exactly (the boundary
  iso-curves share a pole column).
- Split (split_cut_hypothesis): faces partition by mean parameter along
  the around-the-band axis; both hypotheses share the fitted surface
  object and a shared_surface_group tag.
- Branch ambiguity: a projection landing on the coincident boundary curve
  cannot be disambiguated by Newton, the gap re-check, or ValueOfUV (both
  branches are exact). B-spline charts now carry a `home` anchor (the
  projection of the region's mean face centroid) and resolve
  boundary-coincident results to the branch nearer the face's own
  interior; coincidence is verified in 3D so ordinary patch boundaries
  are untouched.
- Compare exemption (stage 3.1): edges whose two faces share a
  shared_surface_group — and corner vertices where such a pair meets —
  are skipped and reported. The exemption is tag-based, never
  tolerance-based: the edge compare is exactly the check that catches
  over-segmentation and stays fully armed for every edge the
  reconstruction did not deliberately create.

The output topology is a deliberate compromise: CAD kernels (and the
reference STEP) write one periodic face with a seam edge. DEVELOPMENT_PLAN
§2.7 gains "Path to the non-compromised design" documenting what that
takes — periodic Interpolate (bound; periodic along U, first row as the
periodic boundary), rescaling the fitted surface's U knots to [0, 2π] so
the existing 2π wrapped-face machinery applies (SetUKnots/SetUPeriodic
bound), the periodic chart flag, seam anchors at azimuth-aligned ring
vertex pairs (irregular walls hit the documented edge-splitting case),
and a periodic chain-repair arm (GeomAPI_Interpolate) — with removing the
compare exemption as the acceptance test.

Results: all 8 tests/nurbs models pass full --compare (elliptical_cylinder
volume within 4.1e-5 of the exact reference; scoreboard 60/65 with only
bad/ failing). Full suite green (477 tests) including a new
elliptical_cylinder stage-2.7 selection test asserting the two-face split
and group tags. Env-gated debug probes (BREPPER_DEBUG_EDGE_UV,
BREPPER_DEBUG_SPLIT) added for chart projections and near-cut partitions.

- **Closed-band detection and seam cut**: a region whose second boundary loop has at least half the extent of the largest is a wrapping band, not a disk-with-hole. It gets cut along a shortest vertex path between the two loops; path vertices are duplicated (the `Region` type now uses local vertex indices to represent clones), and the re-chained boundary marks the two cut copies so corner detection lands exactly at the cut endpoints.
- **One fit, two faces**: the clamped fit over the cut region closes exactly (the duplicated seam column means the two boundary iso-curves share a pole column), and the validated hypothesis splits into two faces sharing that one surface object, tagged with a common `shared_surface_group`.
- **The compare relaxation, kept narrow**: stage 3.1 exempts exactly the tagged seam-cut edges and their corner vertices, and reports what it skipped. It's identity-based, never tolerance-based — the edge compare stays fully armed against real over-segmentation, and the exemption is dead code for every other model.
- **Branch disambiguation**: the predicted numerical hazard showed up on schedule — projections landing on the coincident boundary curve can't be resolved by Newton, the gap re-check, or `ValueOfUV` (both branches are exact). Charts now carry a `home` anchor in their own face's region and resolve boundary-coincident results toward it.

Two debugging surprises worth knowing: the cut path must follow face *perimeter* edges — a path along a quad's split diagonal tears that quad's triangles onto opposite sides and derails the face partition (this was the main bug); and the model's top/bottom rings turn out to be azimuthally misaligned, which the cut handles fine.

Per your second ask, [DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md](DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md) §2.7 now ends with **"Path to the non-compromised design"**: periodic `Interpolate` (bound, periodic along U with the first row as the boundary), rescaling the fitted surface's U knots to [0, 2π] so the existing 2π-hard-coded wrapped-face machinery applies unchanged, the periodic chart flag, seam anchors at aligned ring vertex pairs, and the periodic chain-repair arm — with *removing the compare exemption* named as the acceptance test.
